chapters.summary: Council Member Tiffany Cabán states her pronouns and role as chair of the Committee on Mental Health and Substance Use. She thanks Chairs Narcisse and Farías and recognizes Public Advocate Jumaane Williams and other members joining.
chapters.title: Chair Cabán opens hearing and recognizes attending officials

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Good afternoon and welcome to today's hearing on access to gender-affirming care and associated mental health outcomes for transgender and non-binary youth.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: My name is Councilmember Tiffany Caban.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: My pronouns are she, her.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I'm the chair of the New York City Council's Committee on Mental Health and Substance Use.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you also to Councilmember...

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Narcisse, Chair of Hospitals Committee, and Councilmember Farias, Chair of Women and Gender Equity Committee, for joining our committee in holding this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Before we begin, I'd like to recognize that we are joined by Public Advocate Jumaane Williams, Councilmember Harvey Epstein, Councilmember Simka Felder,

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Councilmember Santus Woso, and Councilmember Areola on Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Today, the committees are convening to discuss access to gender-affirming care in New York City and its role in improving mental health care outcomes for transgender and non-binary youth.

chapters.summary: Cabán says transgender and nonbinary New Yorkers face federal threats and institutional capitulation. She cites research linking affirming care to roughly 60% lower odds of moderate to severe depression and over 70% lower odds of suicidality.
chapters.title: Cabán cites federal attacks and mental health benefits of gender-affirming care

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: It's no secret that transgender and non-binary New Yorkers have recently faced a barrage of threats, challenges, and intimidation from the federal government.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Several institutions in our city have, unfortunately, capitulated to these pressures, and as a city,

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: We are all worse off for it.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Gender-affirming care not only allows individuals to live as their true selves, but it is also strongly associated with improved mental health outcomes for transgender and non-binary people.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Transgender and non-binary youth especially are disproportionately burdened by poor mental health outcomes driven by reduced social support and heightened stigma and discrimination.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Yet research consistently shows that access to gender-affirming interventions is associated with roughly 60% lower odds of moderate to severe depression and over 70% lower odds of suicidality in youth.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: 70% lower odds of suicidality.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: We not only owe it to young transgender and non-binary New Yorkers to provide them with the care that we know can improve their lives and their mental health, but also to protect them from harm.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And at this moment, when so many trans and queer people in our city are seeing their rights being attacked and stripped away by the federal government, and watching institutions that they rely on for their health care buckle under pressure, I stand as a queer New Yorker in solidarity with you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: My commitment to you is that I will do everything in my power to work with you, to keep you safe, and to fight for our collective liberation.

chapters.summary: Cabán describes Intro 949 from Council Member Shulman, Resolution 208 from Council Member Hanif, and her own Resolution 547. She thanks committee and personal staff and passes the mic to Council Member Narcisse.
chapters.title: Cabán outlines three bills on LGBTQI+ resources, anti-bias training, and care access

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Today, we will also be hearing three pieces of legislation relating to our oversight topic.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: One, Introduction 949, sponsored by Councilmember Shulman, which would require the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to create and make available on their website LGBTQI plus health and gender

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: affirming care resources and a searchable map of LGBTQI plus health services.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Resolution 208, sponsored by Councilmember Hanif, which calls on the New York State Legislature to pass and the Governor to sign legislation that mandates all medical students in New York State receive anti-bias training.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And my own legislation, Resolution 547, which calls on the New York State Legislature to pass and the Governor to sign legislation which establishes a gender-affirming care access program to provide support and increase access to gender-affirming care.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I would like to thank the committee staff who worked to prepare for this hearing, as well as my own staff, and I will now pass the mic to Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Oh, and we're joined by Councilmember Aldewall, and now I will pass it over to co-chair, Councilmember Narcisse.

chapters.summary: Council Member Mercedes Narcisse introduces herself as chair of the Hospitals Committee and names the co-chairs. She defines gender-affirming care and describes higher anxiety, depression, and suicidality among transgender and nonbinary youth.
chapters.title: Chair Narcisse opens Hospitals Committee remarks on gender-affirming care

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I am Councilmember Mercedes Narcisse, Chair of Committee on Hospital.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I'm joined by my colleagues, Councilmember Tiffany Caban, Chair of the Committee on Mental Health and Substance Use, and Councilmember Amanda Farias, Chair of the Committee on Women and Gender Equity.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Thank you for joining us today for this oversight hearing on access to gender-affirming care and associated with mental health outcomes for transgender and non-binary youth.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Gender-affirming care is a model of care that includes medical, surgical, mental health, and non-medical.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: services to support and affirm an individual gender identity.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: This type of care can include social affirmation like adopting gender affirming hair, clothing, and names, or medical affirmations such as

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: puberty blockers, hormone therapy, and gender affirming surgeries.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Transgender and non-binary youth experience significantly higher rates of anxiety, depression, mood disorders, and suicidal ideations than their

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: cisgender peers, largely due to stigma, discrimination, and social rejection and barriers to care that this individual's experience.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Research shows that access to gender-affirming care

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: can substantially improve mental health outcome for transgender and non-binary youth.

chapters.summary: Narcisse says the federal government is limiting access and creating challenges for H&H and DOHMH. As a registered nurse and hospital chair, she commits to pushing back and says the hearing will examine services and legislation.
chapters.title: Narcisse warns federal actions threaten local gender-affirming care

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Despite local efforts to support, we know that the federal side is not on our side.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: The federal government is taking actions to limit access to gender-affirming care.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: These actions at the federal level present challenges for health and hospital and DOHMH to continue providing the care that people need and to

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: As a registered nurse and a chair of a hospital committee, I am committed to ensure that every individual in our city get the care they deserve and needs to get through life.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And what we need to do is continue pushing forward and making sure

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: the bigotry around us, the policies that not on our favors for us to continue addressing them.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And today, we look forward to a hearing from New York City Health and Hospitals and DOHMH about the broader state of gender-affirming care

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: access for our youth across the city of New York, including the availability of services at H&H facilities, DOHMH, and the programs and other city-supported efforts.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: We'll also seek their feedback.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: On legislation before the committee.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Together, we must work to ensure that transgender and non-binary youth have access to the care they deserve, and that our local hospital and health department can continue to provide such services.

chapters.summary: Narcisse thanks senior legislative counsel, policy analyst, legislative analyst, and her staff for preparing the hearing. She recognizes joined members and turns the mic to Chair Farías.
chapters.title: Narcisse thanks committee and personal staff for hearing preparation

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Before we begin, I'd like to thank committee staff, senior legislative counsel, Ria Ogazarara, a policy analyst, Manu Butt, as well as the committee, Brenu.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Brand new legislative analyst, Raina Lee, welcome.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: For their hard work and

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: preparing for this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I also like to thank my staff, Frank Shea, Courtney Lee, and of course, Droshina Jallo.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I would like to recognize that we have been joined, who else did I miss?

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: We don't miss anybody.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: You got everybody.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So I will now turn it over to Chair Faraz.

chapters.summary: Council Member Amanda Farías introduces herself as chair of Women and Gender Equity. She cites Human Rights Campaign analysis that 27 states plus Puerto Rico passed bans affecting 48% of transgender youth, and a survey showing 87% of trans youth using hormones feared losing access.
chapters.title: Chair Farías frames affirming care as life-saving and under nationwide attack

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Amanda Farias, pronouns she, her, and I get to chair the Committee on Women and Gender Equity.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: We're excited to join the Committee on Mental Health and Substance Abuse and the Committee on Hospitals and their chairs, Chair Caban and Chair Narcisse, for today's oversight hearing on access to gender-affirming care and associated mental health outcomes for transgender and non-binary youth.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: As stated by my colleagues, access to gender-affirming care is a life-saving medical necessity that dramatically improves the mental health and overall well-being of gender-diverse, transgender, and non-binary children and adolescents.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Every child deserves to grow up feeling supported in who they are.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: And supporting transgender and non-binary youth means defending their right to health care.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Currently, access to gender-affirming care for young people is under attack nationwide.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: An analysis by the Human Rights Campaign found that 27 states plus Puerto Rico have successfully passed bans on gender-affirming care for transgender and non-binary youth, affecting 48% of transgender youth nationwide.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: A recent survey found that

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: 87% of transgender and non-binary youth and young people who's used hormones to support their gender transition or expression were concerned about losing access to this care.

chapters.summary: Farías says transgender and nonbinary youth experience higher anxiety and depression. She cites a 2025 Trevor Project survey finding youth unable to access wanted hormones were nearly twice as likely to attempt suicide, and notes major medical associations support affirming care.
chapters.title: Farías cites Trevor Project data and medical consensus supporting affirming care

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: These laws interfere with the ability of transgender youth, their families, and their providers to make the health care decisions that are right for them and access the medical care they need and can have devastating consequences.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: It is well documented that transgender and non-binary children experience anxiety and depression at higher rates than their cisgender peers.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: According to a 2025 survey published by the Trevor Project, transgender and non-binary young people who were unable to access the hormones they wanted were nearly twice as likely to attempt suicide than those who could.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Additionally, four out of 10 transgender and non-binary young people seriously considered attempting suicide in the last year.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: These young people are not inherently at a higher risk of these issues.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Rather, they are in a world that fights their existence at every turn.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: These repeated attacks would weigh on any adult, so it is no surprise that young people feel the effects of a transphobic environment so acutely.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Gender-affirming care is backed by decades of research and supported by every major medical association in the United States, representing more than 1.3 million doctors.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Every person has the fundamental right to access the health care they need without fear of discrimination, prejudice, or barriers to treatment.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: that support their mental, physical, and emotional well-being.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: So today, we'll hear from the administration and we'll ask, how are you ensuring access to gender-affirming care for transgender and non-binary youth in New York City?

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: And where are you ensuring that accessibility for them?

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you to the members of the Committee on Women and Gender Equity who have joined us today.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I'd like to thank our committee staff.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Julia Goldsmith-Pinkham, Katie Selina, and Ali Stauffer, as well as my own staff, Daniel Curtin, for their work on today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you so much, and I'll turn it back over to Chair Caban.

chapters.summary: Cabán turns to Public Advocate Jumaane Williams. Williams thanks the chairs and calls for expanding affirming care through public hospitals, school-based health centers, and community organizations, citing Local Laws 126 and 127 on patient rights and training.
chapters.title: Public Advocate Jumaane Williams urges expanded gender-affirming care access

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And now I'm going to turn the mic over to Public Advocate Jumaane Williams to deliver some remarks.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: As mentioned, my name is Jumaane Williams, Public Advocate of the City of New York.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: I want to thank Chairs Caban, Ferrius, and Narcisse, and the members of the Mental Health and Substance Use, Women and Gender Equity, and Hospitals Committee for allowing me the opportunity to provide a statement.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: New York City has to expand access to gender-affirming health care services through public hospital, school-based health centers, and community organizations serving LGBTQ plus youth.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: In 2025, New York City enacted legislation that I was a sponsor of, Local Law 126 and Local Law 127, which required the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to create and distribute signs dealing with health care rights of transgender patients,

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: including preferred pronouns and respectful treatment, for display across city hospitals and report on training provided by hospitals regarding medical for transgender individuals, respectively.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: The city should also strengthen provider training on culturally competent care, ensure insurance coverage for medically necessary treatments, and

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: and improve coordination between mental health and primary care services.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: In addition, the city should continue protecting patient privacy and resisting efforts that could deter families from seeking care.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: These recommendations align with my longstanding support for health care equity and accountability in public systems.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: The intersection of LGBTQ plus identity in the modern health care system remains defined by systemic barriers and persistent health inequities.

chapters.summary: Williams says LGBTQ+ individuals face higher chronic disease, mental distress, and substance use, worsened by stress. He criticizes medical education for failing to train clinicians in sexual orientation and gender identity care, forcing patients to educate providers or avoid care.
chapters.title: Williams describes LGBTQ+ health disparities and gaps in medical education

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: While overall insurance enrollment has improved, LGBTQ plus individuals, particularly people of more color and transgender adults, face heightened rates of chronic disease, mental distress, and substance use disorders, all of which are exacerbated by stress.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: A critical driver of these disparities is a widespread deficiency in medical education, which frequently fails to equip clinicians with baseline competencies in sexual orientation and gender identity care.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Consequently, patients are routinely forced to choose between educating their own physicians, enduring misgendering and substandard treatment, or avoid the medical system entirely, which creates severe gaps in preventative and responsive public health outcomes.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: When any community avoids regular care, it's bad public health for everyone.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Research demonstrates that access to gender-affirming care is associated with improved mental health outcomes among transgender and non-binary youth.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: A longitudinal study found that youth who received gender-affirming medical care experienced significantly lower rates of depression and suicidality compared with those who did not receive such care.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Improved access may therefore contribute to reduced mental health crisis, greater school engagement, enhanced family stability, and better...

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: overall well-being.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Discrimination, barriers to care, and social stigma contributed to health disparities among transgender individuals.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Government agencies must actively address these inequities through policy and service delivery.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Today we'll hear three pieces of legislation by Councilmember Caban, which I'm a co-sponsor, Councilmember Shulman, and Councilmember Hanif.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: I look forward to hearing from both advocates and the administration about these bills.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Ensuring access to gender-affirming care for transgender and non-binary youth is both a public health and equity issue.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: We must eliminate health care barriers and protect transgender New Yorkers from discrimination.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Expanding affirming health services, strengthening mental health supports, and safeguarding patient privacy can improve outcomes for vulnerable youth while reinforcing New York City's commitment to inclusion, dignity, and evidence-based health care policy.

chapters.summary: Williams says he has been public about his journey and speaks to parents who love their children. He warns against using surgery restrictions to take away broader access, compares it to abortion restrictions, and calls for protecting trans youth.
chapters.title: Williams speaks personally about joining trans youth advocacy

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: I'd also like to add I have been very, very public about my continuing journey on these issues, and I've done that because I want to make sure people join me.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: I am not trans, and I don't have any family members who are.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: But I have spoken to parents who love their children like my wife and I love mine.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: And I've spoken to mothers who love their child, how my mother loved my sister and I.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: And I think it's incumbent upon folks like me to speak out because when my children never replace some issues, I hope they're not fighting alone.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: And I hope people join them in making sure that they are protected.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: And so I want us to all do the same.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: And I don't want people to use surgery, which is the least used.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: medical access to take away access from everyone.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: I saw that happen with abortion.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Late-term abortions are not very prevalent, but they use that to take away rights from all women.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: So let's just make sure that we're really focused on making sure people have what they need to live their best lives historically.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: When people don't like folks, when they're biased against folks, they don't disappear.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: They're just harmed, and their lives are made to be unnecessarily painful.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: So let's reverse that.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Let's make sure that we can have people live, love, and be healthy in their lives just like we'd want anyone else to.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: So access to health care would allow us to do that.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: So I'm so thankful that we're having this hearing today.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: And I'm also always concerned when people are talking more about sports than children who are killing themselves.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: And so let's reverse that conversation and make sure that we're protecting everyone.

utterances.speaker: Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Taylor Brown gives her pronouns and role as inaugural director of the Mayor's Office of LGBTQIA+ Affairs. She thanks the committees and states the administration opposes federal attacks and is alarmed by private providers caving to pressure.
chapters.title: Taylor Brown introduces Mayor's Office of LGBTQIA+ Affairs and opposes federal attacks

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Good afternoon, my name is Taylor Brown.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: I use she, her pronouns.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: I serve as the inaugural director of the Mayor's Office of Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer, Intersex, and Asexual Affairs.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Thank you to Chairs Caban, Narcisse, and Farias, and the members of the Council Committees on Mental Health and Substance Use, Women and Gender Equity, and Hospitals, as well as Public Advocate Williams for holding today's critical hearing.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: My office appreciates the Council's attention to gender-affirming care and associated mental health outcomes for transgender and non-binary youth, and I'm grateful for the opportunity to testify on these issues on behalf of the administration.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: I would like to begin by unequivocally stating that the administration firmly opposes the federal government's attacks on transgender and non-binary people, and we are deeply alarmed by the ways in which private health care providers in New York City have caved to pressure from the federal government.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: New York City is fully committed to continuing to protect, support, and cherish transgender and non-binary New Yorkers of all ages.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Gender-affirming care is a lifeline for many transgender and non-binary young people, and New York City will not leave them without the care that they need.

chapters.summary: Brown describes gender-affirming care as interdisciplinary services for gender dysphoria, citing WPATH Standards of Care 8 and Endocrine Society guidance. She explains individualized treatment including social transition, puberty blockers, and hormone therapy based on age and clinical criteria.
chapters.title: Brown defines gender-affirming care and clinical standards for youth

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Gender-affirming care refers broadly to a set of specific interdisciplinary services, interventions, and treatments provided to individuals living with gender dysphoria.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Almost all major medical associations and leading world health authorities support gender-affirming care for transgender and non-binary youth.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: youth living with gender dysphoria.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Today, the WPATH, World Professional Association of Transgender Health, Standards of Care Version 8, and the Endocrine Society's Endocrine

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Treatment of Gender Dysphoric Gender Incongruent Persons are the most widely accepted clinical protocols and policies for the treatment of gender dysphoria in both adult and youth patient populations.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Recently, there has been much fear-mongering propaganda and intentional mischaracterization about gender-affirming care for transgender and non-binary young people.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: It is important to be clear that gender-affirming care, like all health care, is individualized and patient-centric.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Decisions about gender-affirming care, again, like all health care, are made by the patient, the patient's caregiver in the case of youth and adolescents, and the provider.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Treatment protocols for transgender and non-binary youth are based on age, the onset of endogenous puberty, and the relevant clinical criteria.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: For those who meet certain clinical criteria, treatment may include psychological and psychiatric care, as well as non-medical support in the social transition

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: a transgender or non-binary young person may take, including coming out and informing others about their gender identity and how they would like to be treated, using a gender identity consistent name and pronouns,

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: adopting clothing, grooming, hairstyles, chest binders, and other compression garments, padding, and other forms of gender expression, and using gender identity consistent facilities and spaces in both public and private life.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: For those at the early stages of puberty and older, the introduction of puberty suppressants, commonly referred to as puberty blockers, which pause the development of secondary sexual characteristics that are inconsistent with gender identity.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: And finally, the treatment protocols for those at mid to late adolescent age and older, the introduction of hormone therapy, which allows a transgender or non-binary young person to undergo puberty consistent with their gender identity.

chapters.summary: Brown says opponents falsely claim surgeries are performed on youth at high rates. She cites a 2024 Harvard study finding little to no utilization of gender-affirming surgeries by trans and nonbinary youth, and says mental health risks stem from stigma and lack of support.
chapters.title: Brown rebuts false claims about youth gender-affirming surgeries

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Opponents of gender-affirming care for transgender and non-binary youth often falsely claim that gender-affirming surgeries are being performed on transgender and non-binary youth of all ages and at high rates.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: This is not true.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: While there is limited data available on this specific issue, a 2024 study by researchers at the Harvard T.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Chan School of Public Health found little to no utilization of gender-affirming surgeries by transgender and non-binary youth.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Transgender and non-binary young people living with gender dysphoria have higher rates of depression, anxiety, serious psychological distress, and suicide risk compared to their cisgender peers.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: These mental health risks are not driven by being transgender or non-binary, but by stigma, discrimination, rejection, and a lack of supportive services.

chapters.summary: Brown shares 2023 survey data showing suicidal ideation among trans 42%, nonbinary 38%, other gender identity 45%, and questioning 28% students versus 16% cisgender. Suicide attempts were trans 49%, nonbinary 29%, other 33%, questioning 61%, and cisgender 9%.
chapters.title: Brown presents NYC Youth Risk Behavior Survey mental health disparities

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: I would like to share some data points from the Youth Risk Behavioral Survey conducted by the Health Department in 2023 that illustrate the mental health challenges that transgender and non-binary youth in New York experience.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: In 2023, public high school students who identified as transgender

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: 42% and non-binary 38%.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: 8%, some other gender identity at 45% or questioning at 28% were more likely to report suicidal ideation when compared to those identified as cisgender at only 16%.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Those who identified as transgender, 49%, non-binary, 29%, and some other gender identity, 33%, or questioning, at 61%, were more likely to report attempting suicide.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Compared to their cisgender peers, who had a rate of 9% of reporting attempting suicide.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Evidence has shown that when transgender and non-binary youth have access to the gender-affirming care they need, their mental health and overall well-being improve.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Access to gender-affirming care is thus essential health care for the youth who need it.

chapters.summary: Brown describes federal executive orders, funding cuts, investigations, and regulatory actions. She says NYU Langone, Mount Sinai, and New York Presbyterian began ceasing youth gender-affirming care in early 2025, and Mount Sinai and NYU later entered DOJ settlements to end puberty blockers and hormone therapy.
chapters.title: Brown details federal pressure and hospital capitulations in New York City

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: The federal government has waged an all-out campaign against transgender and non-binary people, especially our youth and their health care.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Confronted with executive orders, federal funding cuts, federal investigations, and regulatory policies across the nation and here in New York and New York City, providers of gender-affirming care for transgender and non-binary youth

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: have begun ceasing the provision of care and discharging their patients.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Notably, in New York City, three major providers of gender-affirming care for transgender and non-binary youth, NYU Langone, Mount Sinai, and New York Presbyterian, began ceasing their provision of care in early 2025 following one of the first presidential executive orders.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Over the last three weeks, both Mount Sinai and NYU Langone, in the face of federal investigative subpoenas, entered into settlement agreements with the U.S.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: United States Department of Justice, agreeing seemingly to end the provision of puberty blockers and hormone therapy to transgender and non-binary youth for the treatment of gender dysphoria permanently.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: This has resulted in immense fear, harm, and significant breaches of trust in the transgender and non-binary community.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: It has also resulted in an increased vacuum for care for transgender and non-binary youth here in our city and for those who come to our city seeking care.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Mayor Mamdani, Commission on Human Rights Commissioner and Chair Christine Clark, and I have all spoken out on private medical institutions who have capitulated to the federal administration.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: On September 9th, I spoke at a rally outside of Mount Sinai, criticizing their settlement with the Department of Justice.

chapters.summary: Brown says the Mamdani administration announced a $15 million, three-year investment. It includes a direct care access fund, a confidential health department call and chat line, research on access gaps, gender marker change support, and coordination and evaluation.
chapters.title: Brown announces $15 million city investment in gender-affirming care

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: The Mamdani administration has been and remains committed to ensuring that transgender and non-binary youth are able to access their medically necessary gender-affirming care.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: In June 2026, we announced a proactive $15 million investment to protect, ensure, and expand access to gender-affirming care for young transgender and non-binary New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: This investment, spread across three years, provides emergency funding to directly support providers of gender-affirming care for trans and non-binary youth, connect trans and non-binary New Yorkers to care, and to fund research amid these escalating federal attacks.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: This funding is broken down into the following three initiatives.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: The majority of the funding will go to a direct care access fund for providers of youth gender-affirming care.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: The Department of Health will implement a new fund to support qualified providers of pediatric

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: gender-affirming care in their provision of care to youth patients and to address financial shortfalls resulting from any denials or reductions in federal funding.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: This funding will ensure the continuity of care for medically necessary puberty blockers and hormone therapy for transgender and non-binary youth in accessible and affordable care settings.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: The city will also launch a confidential and dedicated call and chat line at the health department that will link people to available services related to gender-affirming care in New York City in real time.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: The city will also fund research to identify gaps in health care access and outcomes.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: The health department will conduct a mixed method research grounded in partnership with academic and community experts.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: We welcome the opportunity to discuss partnerships with you all.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: The funding will also bolster support for gender marker changes on vital records through the Department of Health, as well as support for overall coordination, evaluation, and data analyses for the gender-affirming care initiatives that I just went over.

chapters.summary: Brown cites the Trans Rights or Human Rights campaign and a forthcoming rights and resource guide. She says H&H and DOHMH continue providing age-appropriate care, supports Intro 949, and notes existing DOHMH LGBTQ health pages, the Health Care Bill of Rights, and NYC Health Map. She then transitions to H&H testimony.
chapters.title: Brown outlines rights guide and city services, supports Intro 949

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Building on the Trans Rights or Human Rights campaign that the administration previously launched to provide education and resources to transgender and non-binary New Yorkers about their legal and civil rights, including in healthcare,

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: my office is finalizing a comprehensive rights and resource guide that we hope to publish as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: The administration will continue to work across agencies to ensure that transgender and non-binary New Yorkers are informed, protected, and served, especially during these unprecedented times.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Critically, the city continues to provide age-appropriate gender-affirming

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: care through services offered by both the Department of Health and NYC Health and Hospitals.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: And finally, I want to thank Councilmember Shulman for putting forward Intro No.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: We support this bill and agree it is critical to provide information and resources to LGBTQI New Yorkers about health care services that are available to them.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: The Health Department already has several resources for LGBTQI New Yorkers, including a suite of webpages, the LGBTQ Health Care Bill of Rights,

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: and the Pride and Care Health Tips for Transgender and Gender Nonconforming and Nonbinary People booklet, available on the Health Department's website in 13 languages.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: The Health Department's NYC Health Map is currently available online as well.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: LGBTQI New Yorkers seeking care can search the Health Map by LGBTQ Services and more.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: My colleagues from the Health Department have a few points to clarify in the bill language and look forward to discussing the bill further.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Thank you again for the opportunity to provide this testimony.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: I look forward to discussion today and answering any questions helpful to the Council on these issues.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: And I will turn it over to my colleagues from the Department of Health.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Or, sorry, health and hospitals?

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Sorry, health and hospitals.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: We've met on Zoom, but it's never the same in person.

chapters.summary: Dr. Andrew Wallach introduces himself as Ambulatory Care Chief Medical Officer at NYC Health and Hospitals, joined by Dr. Omar Fattal. He describes H&H's safety-net mission and history, including 2011 mandatory LGBTQ+ training and the 2014 Metropolitan Pride Health center.
chapters.title: Dr. Andrew Wallach presents H&H mission and LGBTQ+ care history

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Taylor.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Good afternoon to Chairwomen Caban, Narcisse, and Farias, and members of the Committees on Mental Health and Substance Use, Hospitals, and Women and Gender Equity.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: I am Dr.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Andrew Wallach, the Ambulatory Care Chief Medical Officer at New York City Health and Hospitals.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: I am joined today by my colleague, Dr.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Omar Fattah, the Chief Behavioral Health Officer at Health and Hospitals.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: As the public safety net healthcare system, Health and Hospitals'mission is simple.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: To provide comprehensive health services equally to all New Yorkers, regardless of their ability to pay, and to deliver the highest quality care with compassion, dignity, and respect.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Furthermore, we aim to promote and protect health in its fullest sense, the total physical,

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: mental, and social well-being of the people of New York City.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify before you today.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Health and Hospitals has continuously prioritized support for the LGBTQ plus patients and staff in keeping with our values, relevant laws, and regulations.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: In 2011, Health and Hospitals became the first U.S.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Municipal health care system to mandate LGBTQ plus treatment.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: for all staff members, and we continuously provide trainings on LGBTQ plus mental health through e-learnings and live training programs that focus on culturally responsive care.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: In 2014, Health and Hospitals Metropolitan became the first municipal hospital to open a health care center specifically dedicated to the needs of LGBTQ plus patients.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Today, Health and Hospitals operates these Pride Health clinics in eight of its facilities, including Bellevue, Elmhurst, Gotham Health Gouverneur,

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Gotham Health Judson, Jacoby, Lincoln, Metropolitan, and Woodhull.

chapters.summary: Wallach says H&H treats each patient as a whole person and gender-affirming care is not one-size-fits-all. Providers use informed consent with patients and families, make behavioral health referrals, use correct pronouns, create safe spaces, and document in gender-affirming ways.
chapters.title: Wallach describes H&H gender-affirming care and behavioral health integration

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Regardless of the type of care a patient comes to health and hospitals for, we treat each patient as a whole person,

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: working with them to support their physical, mental, and social well-being within the context of best clinical practices and regulatory authority.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: We know gender-affirming care does not have a one-size-fits-all approach, and health and hospital providers, with informed consent,

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: work closely with patients and their families and or legal guardians to equip them with the tools they need to provide the necessary mental and emotional support throughout their gender-affirming health care journey.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: As clinically necessary, health and hospitals medical teams will make referrals to behavioral health teams to

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: ensure minors are getting the care that safeguards their mental well-being, as well as ensuring that our patients'physical needs are equally met.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: All of our behavioral health providers have the training and skills to address the needs and provide care to all of our patients, and this includes providing gender-affirming care.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: To do so, we use the patient's correct pronoun, create a safe space for non-cisgender person to explore their gender expression, and document

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: in our medical records in a gender-affirming manner.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: We work with families to support and work through gender-related issues when they come up in treatment.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Additionally, Health and Hospitals offers the LGBTQ plus mental health training, which is an annual voluntary course facilitated by the Institute of Human Identity.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: The curriculum informs mental health providers on key social determinants that impact the LGBTQ plus population and best practices in delivering affirming psychotherapy to this community.

chapters.summary: Wallach describes the Elmhurst Suicide Prevention and Youth Program, Trans Health Fest, and training referencing WPATH Standards of Care 8. He says all eligible H&H facilities have earned LGBTQ+ Healthcare Equality Leader designations and long-term care facilities earned equality leader recognition. He closes promising care without exceptions.
chapters.title: Wallach highlights community partnerships, training, and H&H designations

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Additionally, we partner with our communities to offer localized support whenever possible.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: For example,

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: The Elmhurst Suicide Prevention and Youth Program offers free workshops and services to schools, community-based organizations, and agencies across Queens with the goal of reducing the rates of suicide for youth.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: While this program primarily meets with youth ages 12 to 24, with an emphasis on Black, Indigenous, and people of color,

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: as well as the LGBTQ plus youth in Queens, additional workshops are available to family and staff from other local organizations.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Also, Health and Hospitals is a co-sponsor of Trans Health Fest, which connects transgender, gender diverse, and non-binary New Yorkers to health care,

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: legal and social support resources here in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Providers at health and hospitals receive extensive training to ensure they are delivering culturally responsive care,

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: to meet the referenced physical, mental, and social needs of minors seeking gender-affirming care.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: These trainings include references to the World Professional Association for Transgender Health Standards of Care Version 8 guidance, which was developed by global professionals across medical and sociological fields

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: to provide clinical guidance to healthcare professionals supporting transgender and gender diverse individuals throughout their healthcare journey.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: This guidance uplifts Health and Hospitals'mission to promote and protect health in its fullest sense and bring the highest level of comprehensive care into our exam rooms.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Health and Hospitals is proud to have received designations from leading national benchmarking organizations for inclusive policies, best practices, and equitable treatment and inclusion.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: All 18 health and hospitals eligible facilities earned the LGBTQ plus healthcare equality leader designation in the Human Rights Campaign Foundation's Healthcare Equity Index.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: This is a recognition that these facilities have received every year since 2015.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Additionally, all five of Health and Hospital's long-term care facilities earned the LGBTQ plus long-term care equality leader designation in the Human Rights Campaign Foundation and SAGE's

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: long-term care equality index in 2025.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Above all, Health and Hospitals recognizes the importance of both being an innovator and an advocate to ensure that every person, youth or otherwise, who walks through our doors is treated with compassion,

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: dignity, and respect when seeking gender-affirming care.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: With our purpose to care for all New Yorkers, Health and Hospitals will continue to meet each patient where they are to achieve these goals.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: No exceptions.

utterances.speaker: Andrew Wallach
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify today on this most important topic.

chapters.summary: Cabán cites peer-reviewed studies and guidance from the American Academy of Pediatrics and Endocrine Society. Taylor Brown defers to DOHMH, whose staff are sworn in; Marnie Davidoff cites a 2022 study of 104 youth and a 2023 study of 300 youth showing lower depression, self-harm, and suicidality.
chapters.title: Cabán asks administration about strongest evidence linking affirming care to mental health

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your testimony and for being here.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I'm going to just start off with some questions around clinical evidence and research.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: The clinical literature, and this was touched upon in your testimony, but including studies published in peer-reviewed journals and guidance from the American Academy of Pediatrics and the Endocrine Society,

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: consistently associates access to gender-affirming care with meaningful reductions in depression, anxiety, and suicidality amongst transgender youth.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: What does DOHMH, what does the administration understand to be the strongest available evidence on the relationship between access to gender-affirming care and mental health outcomes for

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: TGNB youth, and how does that evidence inform the agency's public health guidance?

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Council member, we have representatives from DOHMH who will be responding to the question and answer portion.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Oh, great.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Yeah, they can come up now.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: We're at that pace.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Yeah, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Apologies.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: We just have to swear you in also.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: It's super quick.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Will you please raise your right hand?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Do you affirm to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth before these committees and to respond honestly to council member questions?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Did you have separate testimony you wanted to give?

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Okay, great.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Perfect.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Then you can dive right in.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: Fantastic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: My name is Marnie Davidoff.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: I am the Assistant Commissioner for the Bureau of Children, Youth, and Families and Developmental Disabilities at the New York Department of Health and Mental Hygiene.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: So in response to your question, as so many of the council members have spoken about today, we know that there's overwhelming evidence that when

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: transgender and non-binary youth have appropriate access to individualized gender-affirming care, their mental health is improved.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: In 2022, there was a prospective study.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: Of 104 young people aged 13 to 20 who identified as transgender or non-binary, and it found that receipt of gender-affirming interventions

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: was associated with a lower odds ratio of moderate to severe depressive symptoms and significantly as well lower odds of self-harm or suicidal thoughts.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: And a 2023 study that tracked 300 youth who identify as trans or non-binary, excuse me, for two years.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: As they were receiving gender-affirming hormone therapy,

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: also showed significant decreases in depression and anxiety.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: And, you know, we really believe firmly that this evidence is critical to shaping the way that we approach health and mental health care for youth

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: and are really using this to inform, you know, some of the planning and work that is ahead of us that was discussed earlier.

chapters.summary: Cabán asks whether denial of puberty blockers or hormone therapy elevates suicide risk and whether DOHMH reflects affirming care in suicide prevention planning. Davidoff says yes, citing Trevor Project research and youth suicide prevention efforts focused on marginalized youth.
chapters.title: Cabán asks if DOHMH treats gender-affirming care as suicide prevention

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And you should stay put because my line of questions is mostly for you.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: I'm not going anywhere.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Okay, great.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: So research has also shown that transgender youth who are denied access to puberty blockers or gender-affirming hormone therapy are at significantly elevated risk for suicidal ideation and self-harm compared to those who receive care.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Does DOHMH view access to gender-affirming care as a suicide prevention strategy, and is it reflected in the city's suicide prevention planning?

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: Yes, UHMH absolutely, along with other validated public health sources, views access to gender-affirming care as part of a broader suicide prevention strategy.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: The Trevor Project's research, which was also cited earlier, shows that access to gender-affirming care and gender-affirming environments significantly reduces suicide risk among transgender and non-binary youth.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: And all of our youth suicide prevention initiatives are designed first and foremost to reduce suicide disparities among marginalized youth, and this includes LGBT.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: Q plus youth.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Yeah.

chapters.summary: Cabán asks whether DOHMH has seen utilization changes since federal actions and how it monitors them. Davidoff says 988 counselors are trained on LGBTQ youth needs and referrals, but anonymous, time-limited crisis calls limit demographic tracking.
chapters.title: Cabán questions DOHMH on 988 crisis line data for TGNB youth

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And to that point of suicide prevention strategy, I just want to move to 988 for a second because that's another tool that we have for people of

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: not just different gender identities, but just different experiences, different demographics.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Has DOHMH seen changes in the crisis line or behavioral health service utilization amongst TGNB youth since federal actions began?

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And do you know how it's being monitored at this point?

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: Yeah, thanks for that question.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: So we are very cognizant of the stressors that TGNB individuals are experiencing as a result of federal actions.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: And the, of course, Health Department remains committed to improving LGBTQ health and well-being.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: The 988 counselors do receive specific training on meeting the needs of LGBTQ youth communities and the specialized services that are available to them.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: So if a caller requests LGBTQ plus specialized services, the counselors are able to make that referral.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: And there is also a searchable database online when any New Yorker can use to find services that are affirming.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
utterances.text: And so we only have demographics for a very small number of those callers.

utterances.speaker: Marnie Davidoff
