chapters.summary: Nat Moguet of the New York Transgender Advocacy Group describes cost, housing, transportation, food insecurity, and lack of culturally competent providers. Moguet cites 17.3% of trans New Yorkers reporting cost barriers and 36.2% reporting transportation or housing insecurity, and supports Intro 949, Res 208, and Res 547.
chapters.title: Nat Moguet testifies on barriers to care for TGNC New Yorkers

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: All right, thank you so much, Chair Clarias, Chair Caban, Chair Narcisse, and members of the Committee on Women and Gender Equity, Mental Health and Substance Use, and hospitals for holding this hearing and providing us with the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: My name is Nat Moguet, pronouns they, he, and I'm the Director of Advocacy and Programs at the New York Transgender Advocacy Group, where we focus on creating pathways for TGNC, NBI, New Yorkers to build leadership

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: and drive advocacy and grow community rooted in collective care and power.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: Although New York State has been established as a safe haven for trans youth, health-related societal barriers still prevent our community members from accessing the care we need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: These barriers include housing insecurity, cost barriers, lack of culturally competent providers, food insecurity, and unreliable transportation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: 17.3% of transgender New Yorkers have reported cost barriers for needed medical care compared to 7.3% of non-LGBTQ.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: individuals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: 36.2% of trans New Yorkers have also reported unreliable transportation and housing insecurity as a barrier to receiving health care versus 17.1% of non-LGBTQIA individuals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: This gap in accessibility has been exasperated by hateful rhetoric by the federal administration, placing providers and TGNC and BI clients under extreme fear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: Healthcare should be universal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: However, we are living without a system that guarantees medical coverage for all residents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: Even as a 27-year-old trans activist, I have been without a healthcare provider for four years now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: No PCP, no dentist, none of that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: There's a major shortage of providers who understand our communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: Nearly one-third of LGBTQ New Yorkers report that there are too few health care providers trained in LGBTQ issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: And amongst trans and gender nonconforming New Yorkers, more than half identified the lack of LGBTQ trained providers as a significant barrier.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: This shortage places an unfair responsibility on patients, and TGNC-NBI people frequently have to educate their own health care providers about our bodies, our medications, and our basic health care needs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: And a patient should not have to become a medical educator simply to receive competent care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: We all know that there's been moves towards shuttering health care for our community, and there are clear attempts to restrict our access to safe and affirming resources.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: These moves will be detrimental.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: and deadly towards our community members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: And while opponents try to restrict access and instill fear, our city has the opportunity to remain a leader and dedicated to our people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: We make the following recommendations to the city council and urge support for the following to prioritize constitutional and legal protections for our community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: We support Intro 949, we support Resolution 0208, and we support Resolution 0547.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: Thank you for allowing us to testify, and we look forward to working with you to make sure that trans folks get the support they deserve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nat Moguet
utterances.text: And I will also email over my testimony alongside our trans youth that we have here and provide my contact information.

utterances.speaker: Taylor Brown
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Maxima Rodas, a NYTAG program participant, describes being misgendered despite ID changes and clinics not training front desk staff to relay affirming information. She notes overlooked conditions like diabetes, cancer, and heart disease, and barriers for immigrants and undocumented people; she supports Intro 949. Cabán thanks her and notes Council Member Gutierrez joined.
chapters.title: Maxima Rodas describes misgendering and barriers as a trans woman with HIV

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Amanda C.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: Farias, Chair Tiffany Caban, Chair Mercedes Narcis, and members of the Committee on Women and Gender Equity, the Committee on Mental Health and Substance Abuse, and the Committee on Hospitals for holding this hearing

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: and providing us the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: My name is Maxima Rodas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: I use the pronoun she, they, and I'm a program participant on New York Transgender Advocacy, NITAC.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: Based on my personal experience with the healthcare system in New York City,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: I can say that on numerous occasions, even after deciding to begin my transition and having female listed on all my identification documents, I've been faced situations where I was misgendered.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: Staff at many institutions and clinics are still not trained to properly relay affirmative information from the front desk to the healthcare professionals we are seeking care from.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: Within the scope of what it is understood and known regarding affirmative care,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: There are many other factors involved that are often overlooked, such as diagnosis for diabetes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: cancer, high blood pressure, and cholesterol, heart problems, and skyrocketing numbers of mental health cases, and much more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: Alongside this, many people in our TGNC MB community are immigrants, undocumented, vulnerable,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: marginalized, discriminated against, and criminalized.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: When it comes to healthcare and public services, they face formidable barriers, including fear and lack of services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: To take my own case as an example, I'm 52 years old,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: And I've been living with HIV for over 33 years on ART treatment for the past 16 years, and I have other conditions requiring constant medication, evaluation, and checkups.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: While I'm fortunate enough to have a place to live,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: Others who lack housing face overwhelming stressful situations and constant strain of contending with a system that often offered no help at all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: It is a system designed to make access difficult.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: Or one that is accessible only to privileged few.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: I support the passage of Intran 949 because of a major impact it will have on fall

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: like myself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: I would like to thank the Committee on Women and Gender Equity and the Committee on Mental Health and System Use for the opportunity to testify,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: as through these testimonies we are also sharing the experiences of others who may not be present here today, but who do have a voice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maxima Rodas
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Oh, and we've been joined by Councilmember Gutierrez.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: All right, whenever you're ready.

chapters.summary: Filament Kind describes past hospitalizations for self-injury and finding care at Callen Lorde, now two years on testosterone. Kind says word-of-mouth access creates gaps and Intro 949 would help others find life-saving care; supports Intro 949, Res 208, and Res 547. Cabán thanks the advocates and youth submitting written testimony.
chapters.title: Filament Kind says gender-affirming care is suicide prevention and supports Intro 949

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Amanda C.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: Farias, Chair Tiffany Caravan, Chair Mercedes Narcisse, and members of the Committee on Women and Gender Equity, the Committee on Mental Health and Substance

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: and the Committee on Hospitals for holding this hearing and providing us with the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: My name is Filament Kind, my pronouns are they, he, and I'm a program participant at the New York Transgender Advocacy Group,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: where we focus on creating pathways for TGNC, NBI New Yorkers to build leadership, drive advocacy, and grow community rooted in collective care and power.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: I am here today to explain why I believe Intro 949 is an essential step towards guaranteeing the health and safety of trans New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: Six years ago, I was hospitalized after coming very close to ending my own life and engaging in self-injurious behaviors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: Four years ago, I did so again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: My life then felt like a maze with no end.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: I was lost.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: I did not know who I was, and I didn't feel like I fit anywhere I found myself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: I'd known for many years that I was queer and trans, but a piece was still missing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: For me, that missing piece was medical transition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: Luckily, in 2023, I made a friend, Joe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: Who guided me to community health clinics where I could receive the gender-affirming care I was seeking when I did not know where else to turn or where to start.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: Once I made my first appointment at Callen Lord, I knew for certain that starting HRT was what I wanted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: I am now two years on testosterone, and I can say without a doubt that testosterone and queer joy have been the most effective antidepressants that I've ever been on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: Gender-affirming care is suicide prevention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: Now, some trans folks in New York City may not be so lucky.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: I am an English-speaking white U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: Citizen, so finding queer community was easier for me to access.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: This information is primarily spread by word of mouth, creating gaps in access to this crucial health care for those who don't have such community or connections yet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: Intro 949 would create for many of these folks access to health care that could save lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: We thank the Committee on Women and Gender Equity, the Committee on Mental Health and Substance Use, and the Committee on Hospitals for their continued support and leadership in protecting TGNC-NBI New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: We make the following recommendations to City Council and urge support for the following to prioritize constitutional and legal protections for TGNC-NBI folks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: We support Intro 949 to create a resource map related to the unique health care needs of LGBTQI individuals, including information regarding access to health services and obtaining and providing gender-affirming care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: We support Resolution 0208, mandating all medical students in New York State to receive anti-bias training.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: We support Resolution 0547 to establish a gender-affirming care program in the Department of Health to ensure the continuity of gender-affirming care services in the state.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: We thank the Committee on Women and Gender Equity and the Committee on Mental Health and Substance Use for its continued support and leadership in protecting TGNC NBI New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: Thank you for allowing us to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: And we look forward to working with you to make sure trans folks get the support they deserve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you for your advocacy even more so.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you for sharing your deeply, deeply personal stories.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And I just want to say to the young folks who have joined us and are submitting written testimony, I cannot wait to read it.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And thank you so, so much for engaging in this process.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: What you bring to us, we take incredibly seriously, and we're going to do everything possible to be as supportive as we can.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: So thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Okay.
