chapters.summary: Ocean D. Waves, a 20-year-old Afro-Latino transgender man, describes homelessness and daily testosterone as essential care. He describes biochemical dysphoria and says Intro 949 would expand access to gender-affirming, dental, primary, reproductive, and mental health care; supports all three measures.
chapters.title: Ocean D. Waves testifies as homeless trans man about hormones and access

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: Hi, my name is Ocean D.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: Waves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: I'm 20 years old.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: My pronouns are he, him.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: Fascism depends on complicity and violence, both physical and non-physical.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: Three private hospitals, Mount Sinai, NYU Langone, and NY Presbyterian have halted or restricted gender-affirming care for trans youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: This should provoke rage across communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: One of fascism's central tools is desensitization to the heinous.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: To view something so beautifully complex and so deeply human as being transgender as though if it were a crime is inhumane.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: A person's right to exist should not be dictated by anyone but themselves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: I am an Afro-Latino transgender man, and I am homeless.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: When I wake up every morning, right after I get out of the shower, my routine is the same.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: I put my tea gel on each shoulder.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: That's how I start my day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: This is not optional or abstract.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: It is how I care for myself, how I move through the world, how I be myself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: My hormones make the challenges of being homeless so much easier.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: I go out into the world with a clearer mind than I ever had, a confidence that flows wherever I stand, and a self-love that I wouldn't have otherwise known.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: A beautifully complex journey of understanding my gender, breaking boxes is what it means to be transgender.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: Prior to hormones, I was not present in my body, no matter how much I forced myself to live with myself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: My subconscious always knew that hormones were what I needed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: Biochemical dysphoria is not something known to many.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: Biochemical dysphoria is caused by not having the right hormones in your body.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: I had biochemical dysphoria and I was miserable beyond belief.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: It has been proven time and time again that gender-affirming care is the solution, that gender-affirming care keeps us alive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: Gender-affirming care lets us experience life like our cisgender counterparts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: Intro 949 will address these challenges and it will benefit me, my community, and my loved ones by providing them equal opportunity and access to medical care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: Examples of this include gender-affirming care, dental care, primary health care, reproductive care, mental health care, and beyond.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: To deny gender-affirming care is to deny science.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: It's complacency and genocide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: We are trans youth, elders, and adults, all who just want to go outside and freely be themselves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: No one should be denied the right to be free.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: We support INT 0949-2026 Showman to create a resource map related to the unique health care needs of LGBTQI individuals, including the information regarding access to LGBTQI health.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: services and obtaining and providing a gender-affirming care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: We support RES 0208-2026, mandating all medical students in New York State receive anti-bias training.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: We support RES 0547-2026 to establish gender-affirming care program in the Department of Health to assure gender-affirming care services in the state.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: We thank the Committee on Women and Gender Equity, the Committee on Hospitals, and the Committee on Mental Health and Substance Use for the opportunity they have given me to be able to use my voice to help my community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: We appreciate your continued support and contributions in regards to the protection of TGNC and B New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: Trans folks will know the community has their back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: We are only as strong as our community makes us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: I'm going to make a year on T in two days.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: This has been the best year of my entire life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: The ability to be unapologetically human is a human right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Filament Kind
utterances.text: Whenever you're ready.

chapters.summary: Zev Frank, a Youth Advocacy Fellow at NYTAG, says even supportive parents were lost trying to help with hormone replacement therapy. He describes misinformation and fear when searching for trans health care and says city-verified resources through Intro 949 would reduce doubt; supports Intro 949, Res 208, and Res 547.
chapters.title: Zev Frank describes difficulty finding trustworthy trans health information

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Farias, Chair Caban, Chair Narcisse, and members of the Committee on Women and Gender Equity, the Committee on Mental Health and Substance Use, and the Committee on Hospitals for holding this hearing and providing us with an opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: My name is Zev Frank, a Youth Advocacy Fellow at NITAG.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: I am a young transgender community member with lived experience on how frightening and confusing it can be trying to find information about TGNC and B health services and gender affirming care that is accurate and approachable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: It's going to be incredibly difficult, especially for a young person with no experience in handling their own health care, trying to find this information by themselves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: Even for those of us who have allies in our lives that support us, it doesn't mean that they know everything about our needs or health.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: When I needed dental work done, I talked to my parents, and they helped me find a dentist, deal with insurance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: When I needed hormone replacement therapy, they were more lost and confused than I was.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: Like so many people, I had to extensively search for the resources I needed on the internet, and it was daunting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: There is so much misinformation out there and a lack of accurate information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: As a TGNCNB person, it can be scary trying to find medical information and practitioners you can trust.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: If I had verified information and resources from the city during my search, it would have taken away so much of that doubt and fear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: I was eventually fortunate enough to be able to find a doctor I can trust who is both welcoming and knowledgeable about transgender health care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: At 25 and after over six years of medically transitioning,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: I am still learning vital information about my own reproductive health due to a lack of access to relevant resources.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: Alongside this, most medical professionals I have seen either didn't know or did not provide a safe environment for me to ask.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: Access to safe, affirming health care is vital to individuals in the TGNCNB community and can be genuinely life-saving.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: Making this information more accessible to those in NYC who need it through legislation like Intro 949 will undoubtedly be life-changing for many.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: We thank the Committee on Women and Gender Equity and the Committee on Mental Health and Substance Use for its continued support and leadership in protecting TGNCNB New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: Thank you for allowing us to testify, and we look forward to working with you to make sure trans folks get the support they deserve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: We make the following recommendations to the City Council and urge support for the following to prioritize constitutional legal protections for TGNC and BI folks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: We support Intro 949 to create a resource map related to the unique health care needs of LGBTQI plus individuals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: We support Resolution 0208 and we support Resolution 0547.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Ellis Jablonski says Mount Sinai called about handing over trans patient records to the federal administration, which he called a privacy violation. He also describes misgendering, deadnaming, and an unsolicited procedure pitch at an orthodontist; supports Intro 949, Res 208, and Res 547.
chapters.title: Ellis Jablonski recounts Mount Sinai privacy scare and provider bias

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Farias, Chair Caban, Chair Narcisse, and members of the Committee on Women and Gender Equity, the Committee on Mental Health and Substance Use, and the Committee on Hospitals for holding this hearing and providing us with the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: My name is Ellis Rejablonski.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: I use pronouns he, him.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: I'm a program participant at the New York Transgender Advocacy Group.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: Receiving medical care as a trans person does not come with the same guarantee of safety and respect as with our cisgender counterparts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: Earlier this year, I was getting ready to leave the house when I received a phone call from my former provider, Mount Sinai, who I hadn't been to since 2022,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: that they were under oath to the administration to hand over all the personal information of their trans patients who received gender-affirming care there as minors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: I was furious not only that they could do this because it was a blatant HIPAA and privacy violation, but that the hospital gave in so easily to pressure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: The woman on the phone that I was speaking to insisted that the hospital's hands were tied.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: Ultimately, the information release was deemed unlawful by federal court, but no patient should ever have to have that kind of fear that their doctor could do something like that to them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: This is a unique risk that we as trans patients face when our identity is weaponized into a political talking piece.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: In other adverse medical experiences, I've been misgendered and deadnamed even when the dermatologist's office has a preferred name and pronoun box on the intake paperwork.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: I went to the orthodontist for a...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: Retainer fitting when the doctor unsolicited tried to

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: sell me a phony gender-affirming procedure, cosmetic tooth procedure, when I've just come in for a checkup.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: Health visits can be stressful enough as is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: Having a piece of legislation like Intro 949 will allow people to find health care providers who respect trans patients and prioritize protecting our health and our dignity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: We thank the Committee on Women and Gender Equity, the Committee on Mental Health and Substance Use, and the Committee on Hospitals for their continued support and leadership in protecting TGNC and BI New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: We make the following recommendations to the City Council and urge support for the following to prioritize constitutional and legal protections for TGNC and BI folks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: We support Intro 0949, we support Resolution 0208, and we support Resolution 0547.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: We thank the Committee on Women and Gender Equity and the Committee on Mental Health and Substance Use for its continued support and leadership in protecting TGNC and BI New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: Thank you for allowing us to testify, and we look forward to working with you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Oh, yeah, you can pull it over to your horse, which it's up to you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: There you go.

chapters.summary: Cygnus Pavo, a Youth Advocate Fellow at NYTAG, says trans people struggle to find affordable, reputable, gender-affirming clinics. He describes friends refused hormone therapy at pharmacies and says a DOHMH LGBTQ+ health section would be a vital commitment; supports Intro 949, Res 208, and Res 547.
chapters.title: Cygnus Pavo describes struggles finding affirming primary and mental health care

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Farias, Chair Caban, Chair Naisis, and members of the Committee on Women and Gender Equity, the Committee on Mental Health and Substance Use, and the Committee on Hospitals for holding this hearing, providing us with the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: My name is Cygnus Pavel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: I use they, them pronouns, and I'm a Youth Advocate Fellow at the New York Transgender Advocacy Group.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: As a trans person who is currently receiving gender-affirming care, I've struggled in the past and still struggle now to find a healthcare provider that fits my needs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: I personally had to search long and hard to find a gender-affirming clinic that is not only accessible, but affordable and reputable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: Receiving gender-affirming care in any form, from hormone therapy to affirming surgeries, is an extensive process and it will affect every other type of healthcare you receive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: I am currently struggling to find primary care physicians that I know will not discriminate against me because I am medically transitioning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: I've had friends in the past who went to CVS or any other major pharmacy to pick up their hormone therapy, only for them to be interrogated and even outright refused their medication.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: I have even more friends that can't access gender-affirming care because of affordability issues or not being able to access knowledge regarding clinics that will accept their insurance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: Trans people, even in New York City, which is considered a safe haven, struggle to find places to receive health care without facing discrimination.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: Across the U.S., gender-affirming care is being outlawed, and private hospitals such as Mount Sinai and NYU Langone are capitulating to the federal administration and restricting who can receive care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: Having a portion of the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene's website dedicated to LGBTQ plus healthcare would be a vital commitment to NYC's LGBTQ plus citizens, a commitment that is very defined in this political climate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: We support Insure 949 to create a resource map related to the unique healthcare needs of LGBTQI plus individuals, including information regarding access to LGBTQIS health services and attaining and providing gender-affirming care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: We support Resolution 0208, mandating all medical students in New York State to receive anti-bias training, and we support Resolution 0547 to establish a gender-affirming care program in the Department of Health to ensure the continuity of gender-affirming care services in the state.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: We thank the Committee on Women and Gender Equity and the Committee on Mental Health and Substance Use for its continued support and leadership in protecting transgender, gender nonconforming, and non-binary New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: Thank you for allowing us to testify, and we look forward to working with you to make sure trans folks get the support they deserve.

chapters.summary: Cabán invites the panel to suggest additional city actions. Cygnus Pavo says the hardest part of receiving care is finding therapists or providers aware of transgender struggles and asks for improved mental health and psychiatric care access.
chapters.title: Cabán asks panel what else city government can do; Cygnus Pavo prioritizes mental health access

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you so, so much for being here and for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Actually, I have a question for you all, and I'm putting you on the spot, so if you can't think of it now, I just want to invite you to follow up with me, with my colleagues, so that we can be in conversation around it.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: But I'm just wondering, you know, it's clear that you all support the three pieces of legislation that we heard about in the hearing today, but do you think that there are other things that the city government...

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Could or should be doing to better support you and the folks in your community.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Ignore that.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And any one of you can jump in.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Any and all of you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: I guess for me, the hardest part of receiving care has definitely been mental health care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: It's hard to find a therapist or a provider that is gender, is aware of the struggles of a transgender person.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: And so I really would like to see if there's any way to improve access to mental health care for transgender people, especially since our health and our mental safety is really being tested in this political climate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cygnus Pavo
utterances.text: So I think definitely just improving access to mental health and psychiatric care would be really helpful.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Ocean D. Waves says government should stop erasing trans and queer history, citing the removal of a Marsha P. Johnson monument. Cabán agrees and discusses increasing representation, monuments, and funding for queer and trans artists.
chapters.title: Ocean D. Waves urges city to preserve trans and queer history

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Is there anybody else?

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: Something that I would like to see changed government-wise is for the government to stop erasing trans and queer history.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: There was a Marsha P.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: Johnson monument, and they took that down, and they pretend like trans people or queer people just don't exist, and we do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: We always have throughout time, throughout history.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: And erasing our history doesn't erase the people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: So I and just us as a collective would really appreciate if people put focus on history, transgender and queer history, because that's important.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ocean D. Waves
utterances.text: We need it to move forward.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And I really, really appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: It's obviously part of the playbook, and that's well heard.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And it's something we're pursuing to make sure that we are increasing the number of representation in our cultural institutions, that we're adding more monuments, and more than that, knowing that we're creating history right now, and so we need to put money in the...

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: In the hands of queer and trans artists and just people that are doing incredibly good work.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And, you know, it goes all the way back even to Nazi Germany.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Like, in addition to persecuting Jews, the first thing they did was loot and put on fire all of the research that had been done in

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: the premier center for sexual and gender health that they were doing in Germany at the time.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: So that is really well noted and taken.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: So thank you for that.

chapters.summary: Zev Frank says trans people need safe practitioners for binding and other aspects of life, not only gender-affirming care. He says being visibly or openly trans can affect care even at a dentist or outside gender-affirming settings.
chapters.title: Zev Frank asks for safe, reliable care beyond gender-affirming treatment

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Does anybody else want to add?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: I think I just want to add, especially if they're talking about, you know, safe, like, reliable health care for transgender people, I think that can go beyond,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: you know, like, gender-affirming care and also just, like, when it comes to, like, binding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: Safe medical practitioners to go to, or in so many aspects of life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: But I think this is one where people can be very vulnerable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: I know in my experiences, and I've heard other people say this too, experiences with medical practitioners, even a dentist, something outside of seeking gender-affirming care, it can be...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zev Frank
utterances.text: Visibly or openly trans can really impact the care you receive and it can be really a difficult task trying to find someone you can trust and try to find like safe reliable care.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Ellis Jablonski says the Council listening to trans residents matters. He describes difficulty accessing a gender-neutral restroom at a public pool and urges positive, authentic media representation; Cabán thanks the panel and encourages follow-up.
chapters.title: Ellis Jablonski calls for listening, gender-neutral facilities, and positive media

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: I guess it's difficult to say because just, you know, what's even within the ability and scope of the city council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: I mean, I kind of just what you're doing right now, which is just, you know, listening and actively listening to voices of, you know,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: trans and gender nonconforming residents, I think is really the most important part because

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: You know, obviously, obviously with everything going on right now, and it's just something like today where we're coming in to talk about one aspect of our lives, which is the medical section, but there are other, you know, aspects, like we face

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: difficulty and discrimination in that area, but then there are other areas of our lives as well that we are...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: Just there are not institutional accommodations for, I guess, I guess to give an example, like sometimes I'll use, and this is, I don't know, like, like to give an example, sometimes I'll use the city, uh, exercise recreational facilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: I'll go to the public swimming pool, but I can't really, my ability to use, you know, something like that is like that other people may take for granted is not really, it's been a longstanding issue because there isn't a gender neutral

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: restroom that I, like I would have to go separately to the front desk and then ask them for the key each time to unlock the like single stall and like I might

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: just come out of the pool just like dripping wet and be like hey can you like unlock it just every single time like there's not there isn't that space

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: that's like carved out for us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: And it can make the day to day like frustrating and really grueling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: So it's, yeah, I mean, really, really just being open to input and like you're doing now and really just, because I think

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: Something, and I think the, I really admired the Mayor Mabdani's

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: initiatives where he speaks about this publicly, but I think particularly in the media, there's so much negative and false messaging pertaining to trans people, just,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: you know, spreading completely just fear-mongering that's not based in any form of reality whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: And I think just media, positive media representation and telling authentic and positive stories about trans people, I think is just so important in any shape or form.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: That is...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ellis Jablonski
utterances.text: Yeah, so in the way that I see it, that's the most important.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Y'all are brilliant and powerful, and so just encourage you, please be in touch.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: We'd love to stay in communication, and we're all ears.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And I think Chair Narcisse has a question.

chapters.summary: Narcisse praises the witnesses' strength and leadership. She says their willingness to testify and speak with love will push back against hate and urges them to keep using their voices.
chapters.title: Narcisse encourages youth witnesses to keep advocating

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I was just going to add that your strength.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Willing to testify, willing to have the conversation, is what's going to make, it's just with your love, with driving it, will push out the hate toward anyone else that come behind you.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So you're taking the lead.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: You are leaders and continue being the leader and advocate and make your voice not let no one shadow your voice, but let your voice be out.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: And you have the greatest advocates around here, too.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So keep on coming, telling us, and then we'll be, you know, making sure that we do what we're supposed to do in our end.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Thank you for being here.

chapters.summary: Cabán acknowledges that Council Member Pierina Sanchez joined. She thanks the panel and moves to the next speaker.
chapters.title: Cabán notes Council Member Sanchez joined hearing

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you, guys.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And I just want to acknowledge that we have been joined by Councilmember Pierina Sanchez.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Well, we were joined.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: See you later.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thanks so much.

chapters.summary: Cabán introduces Manhattan Borough President Brad Hoylman-Sigal. He thanks the Council, notes Stonewall, and says at least 27 states restrict gender-affirming care while New York is becoming a safe haven.
chapters.title: Manhattan Borough President Brad Hoylman-Sigal testifies on protecting trans youth

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: All right, next up, we have our Manhattan Borough President, Brad Hoylman-Siegel.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Yeah, you came a long way, Borough Prez.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: I traveled across the street.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: Yes, it's a change from Albany where I have a five-minute commute from Union Square.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: Quite a luxury.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: Chairs Gervon and Arcees and various and members of the Committee on Mental Health and Substance Use, Hospitals, Women and Gender Equality.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: I'm Manhattan Borough President Brad Hoylman-Siegel.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: Proud to represent the borough where the modern LGBTQ plus human rights movement was born at Stonewalls 57 years ago.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: And I really want to thank the council and your leadership for convening this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: And to the families, the young people, providers, and advocates fighting to protect the life-saving medical care that we're discussing today under the threats from the Trump administration.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: I'm extremely proud to stand alongside you.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: You know that we face a targeted campaign to end medical care for transgender youth.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: At least 27 states have enacted bans or laws restricting gender-affirming care for trans youth.

chapters.summary: Hoylman-Sigal describes an expected federal Medicaid and CHIP reimbursement rule, DOJ subpoenas for patient records, and SHIELD Law 2.0 notification protections. He says Lambda Legal, ACLU, and NYLPI won an injunction, and that NYU Langone and Mount Sinai settlements ended youth gender-affirming medical care.
chapters.title: Hoylman-Sigal details SHIELD law, federal subpoenas, and hospital settlements

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: And as

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: As more of the country closes its doors, New York is slowly becoming one of the last safe havens and bastions of health care for the LGBTQ plus community.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: But none of us can take that protection for granted.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: On October 13, the Trump administration is expected to implement a federal rule ending Medicaid and CHIP reimbursement for this care for young people.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: And this year, as we know, the Department of Justice under Trump issued subpoenas to hospitals nationwide, including several here in New York City, seeking the private records of young patients.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: I've heard from so many families whose children's records were among those demanded by these subpoenas.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: It is a uniquely terrifying situation to be in.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: To do everything in your power to make sure your child receives life-saving medical care, and that's what it is, and then to have the federal government violate your children's and your family's rights to medical privacy.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: I had the privilege of working with colleagues in Albany in passing New York's SHIELD law

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: and what's called the SHIELD law 2.0 to provide the strongest possible protections to transgender New Yorkers and their families and medical providers against the abuses in the legal process.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: The SHIELD law 2.0 protects patients and providers from attempts by out-of-state prosecutors.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: To find them liable.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: or seek information in New York simply for providing, seeking, or obtaining life-saving care that is legal in New York State.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: It also requires New York institutions that receive requests for protected health information, even from the federal government, to notify the Attorney General and affected patients before any disclosure.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: Because of the SHIELD Law 2.0, the families whose records were sought by the Trump Department of Justice through federal grand jury subpoenas were at least notified with enough time to get to court.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: With help from Lambda Legal, the ACLU, and Nightclue, they won an injunction, still active today, that blocks the Department of Justice from obtaining these records.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: But as you are well aware, a state law cannot override a federal law and cannot by itself stop a federal investigation.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: It also cannot protect what does not exist.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: We need providers to actually provide care.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: And as the Trump administration continues its crusade, its shameful crusade, there are fewer and fewer willing to do so.

chapters.summary: Hoylman-Sigal calls the settlements federal overreach and quotes a parent saying New York protects its children. He urges passage of Intro 949 and the resolutions, but says the city's $15 million commitment will not cover the impending loss of Medicaid dollars.
chapters.title: Hoylman-Sigal supports Intro 949 but says $15M is insufficient

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: This month, as we know, two of Manhattan's largest hospital systems, NYU Langone and Mount Sinai, reached agreements with the Department of Justice to end youth gender-affirming medical care.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: I think we're all disappointed by this decision and by what they mean for these young people and families who relied on these institutions.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: I'm also greatly concerned that we still do not have clarity on

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: the details of these settlements, including how the hospitals will ensure continuity of care for patients currently undergoing treatment.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: Make no mistake, this is the result of the federal government uniquely obsessed with stopping transgender people from getting health care and stripping away their basic rights.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: But as Dawn Gabriel, the mother of a 17-year-old whose records were included in the grand jury subpoena here in New York, told me, quote, in New York, we protect our children.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: We don't feed them to the beast, especially for political convenience.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: As access to this care declines, families need clear.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: And accurate information about where the care is still available.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: Council Member Shulman's bill, Intro 949, would require DOHMH to publish LGBTQ plus health and gender affirming care resources and maintain a searchable map of these health services.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: I urge you

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: to consider and pass this legislation.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: I also applaud the resolutions before you for Albany to act on similar measures.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: But our work isn't finished.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: I was glad to see the council commit $15 million to providers, but unfortunately, that's still not enough money

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: to cover the impending loss of Medicaid dollars.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: So the city and the state need to do everything in our collective power to meet

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: these needs.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: Thank you again to the council and the advocates in this room today who continue to fight for the right of transgender young people to live and thrive in New York.

utterances.speaker: Brad Hoylman-Sigal
utterances.text: And thank you for the opportunity to testify today.

chapters.summary: Cabán thanks Hoylman-Sigal for his testimony. She announces the next panel: Judith Goldner, Brie Farron, Tatiana Cruz, Alexia Sol, and Ronan Tuggle.
chapters.title: Cabán thanks Borough President and calls next panel

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you, Borough President.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: We really, really appreciate it and also appreciate the good work and the collaboration.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Okay, next up we have Judith Goldner, Brie Farron, Tatiana Cruz, Alexia Sol, and Ronan Tuggle.

chapters.summary: Judith Goldner of the Legal Aid Society says Legal Aid was lead counsel in Cruz v. Zucker and is committed to gender-affirming care. She says Mount Sinai and NYU are dumping patients without continuity, supports Res 547, and is mostly supportive of Intro 949 but warns the map could lead to harassment and threats.
chapters.title: Legal Aid Society's Judith Goldner testifies on litigation and map concerns

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: Anybody can start.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: My name is Judith Goldner.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: I'm the attorney in charge of the Civil Law Reform Unit at the Legal Aid Society, and I want to thank the council for holding this very important oversight hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: I want to start by saying, you know, we at Legal Aid are very committed to ensuring that everyone who has gender dysphoria is

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: given access to the medically necessary care that they deserve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: We were lead counsel in Cruz v.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: Zucker, which was our lawsuit against New York State to ensure gender-affirming care for folks who need that care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: We are obviously very concerned about not just what the Trump administration is trying to do here, but also that hospitals such as Mount Sinai and NYU

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: are dumping patients, they are not providing continuum care, everyone needs to know that that's not what's happening.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: We appreciate that that care is still available for young people at the city hospitals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: We are a bit concerned, however, that

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: The $15 million is not going to go to care for young people, and it's care for young people that is most at risk right now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: So it's super important, I think, for the council to make it clear to the city that it's so critical for the city to continue to provide that care to folks who are not otherwise going to be able to access it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: We support, we're very supportive of Resolution 0547, which calls on the legislature to pass

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: A819 and S7985, which would ensure

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: which would establish a gender-affirming care program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: And we want to make sure that the state is going to continue to provide that care to people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: We are mostly supportive of Intro 0949.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: We are somewhat concerned about the mapping part of this because it could...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: Could lead to harassment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: threats and so we would be happy to work with the council on figuring out ways to you know allow people who should have access to information without

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: opening it up to people who might behave badly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: And thanks again for doing this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: We are always available to help folks with issues as they come up as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And we're eager to be in conversation and hear more.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I'm sure the sponsor of the bill is as well.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Judith Goldner
utterances.text: We will reach out.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Tatiana Cruz of Make the Road New York and the NYC Trans and Queer Coalition says she fled Florida for safety and care. She says affirming care improved her emotional well-being and helped her overcome substance abuse, and describes 17-year-old Jade losing care; supports Res 547 and Res 208.
chapters.title: Tatiana Cruz shares coming to New York for care and a trans girl's disrupted treatment

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you, Chairman Tiffany Caban, the members of the Committee on Mental Health and Substance Abuse, and the New York City Council for holding this important oversight hearing

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: on access to gender-affirming care and associated mental health outcomes for transgender and non-binary youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: My name is Tatiana Cruz.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: I am a trans activist and a member of Make the Road New York and NYC Trans and Queer Coalition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: I fled Florida and came to New York because I needed a place where I can live openly and authentically.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: I needed community, safety, and access to health care that recognized me for who I am.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: Here in New York, I found those things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: Gender-affirming care is medically necessary, evidence-based healthcare recognized by major medical organizations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: This is healthcare and not a political debate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: For me, access to this care has profoundly improved my emotional and psychological well-being.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: It helped me feel comfortable in my body, confident in myself,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: and able to live as the woman that I know myself to be.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: All of these have also helped me even overcome substance abuse.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: This is why this issue is deeply personal to me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: I also think about a young trans girl named Jade, whom I met when she was 12.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: She is now 17.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: I have watched her grow up, but I have also watched her struggle recently after losing access to gender-affirming care that she once received.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: At 17, Jade should be focused on her future, her dreams, her education, and becoming the person that she wants to be.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: She should not have to be struggling because access to her health care was taken away.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: Her story reminds us that access to care cannot depend on where someone lives or on changing political circumstances.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: That is why...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: Yes, that is why New York Trans and Queer Coalition supports Resolution 547 and 208 and its call for a statewide gender-affirming care access program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: We need continuity of care, stable providers, statewide coordination, and long-term investment so transgender New Yorkers can access the health care that they need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: I came to New York because I needed the opportunity to live, heal, and thrive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: And I want Jade and every transgender young person to have the same opportunity without having to leave home to find it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tatiana Cruz
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

chapters.summary: Alexia Sol describes lacking hormone therapy, surgeries, and emotional support as a young trans woman and having two suicide attempts. She urges New York City to invest in gender-affirming care and community health and supports Res 547 and Res 208; Cabán reads the English translation.
chapters.title: Alexia Sol testifies in Spanish on suicide attempts and need for trans youth support

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: I say in Spanish.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Está bien.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Buenas tardes a todos y gracias a la presidenta Tiffany Caban, a los integrantes del Comité de Salud Mental y Uso de Sustancias y al Consejo Municipal de Nueva York por llevar a cabo esta importante audiencia de supervivencia sobre el acceso a la atención de afirmación de género

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: y los resultados asociados de salud mental para jóvenes transgénero y no binarios.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Mi nombre es Alexia Sol, soy activista y miembro de la comunidad de May the Rock New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: En lo personal de joven no tuve acceso a terapia hormonal ni a cirugías, mucho menos acompañamiento.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Tampoco conté con apoyo emocional para transicionar, así que tuve que vivir una vida que no quería realmente.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Es triste decir que tuve dos intentos de suicidio por no saber cómo llevar mi vida como una mujer trans, porque viví una identidad en la cual no me sentía plena y segura.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Esta tarde estoy aquí testificando porque queremos que la ciudad de Nueva York se comprometa a ser parte del cambio y pedirles que no permitan que los jóvenes trans vivan lo que yo viví cuando joven.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Que ninguna infancia trans tenga que sufrir y llorar en un cuarto a solas por no tener a su familia.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: acceso a terapia hormonal y al apoyo, especialmente de la familia y de los especialistas en salud, que estos especialistas cuando obtuvieron sus licencias hicieron un juramento de salvar vidas en vez de permitir que una vida dejara de existir.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Antes de negar el acceso a la terapia hormonal a una persona trans, piensen en lo que esa persona que puede estar viviendo y pensando.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Quizás lo que está en su mente es que no hay salida, que no puede ser quien realmente es.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: En cualquier rincón del país o del mundo, un pequeño ser humano puede estar pensando en rendirse y acabar con su vida hoy, porque la sociedad le está negando el derecho a vivir su proceso de transformación.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: A ser quien realmente es.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Hoy día quiero hablarles directamente a esos jóvenes trans que piensan que están solos.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Quiero recordarles que no lo están, que nos vean a quienes hoy hemos transicionado, que a pesar de que no fue fácil, al final del día nuestras vidas son similares a la metamorfosis de una oruga,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: que se arrastra y lucha contra viento y marea, pero que un día esa oruga se convierte en una hermosa mariposa.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: La coalición hace petición al Consejo de seguir invirtiendo en acceso a la atención médica de afirmación de género para personas sin seguro o con seguro insuficiente.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Que existan organizaciones comunitarias de salud LGBTQ+, servicios de salud mental para jóvenes que la recuperación de datos respete la privacidad y ayude a identificar las deficiencias en los servicios.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: La coalición también apoya fuertemente las resoluciones 547 y 208.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Estas resoluciones brindan a

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: nuestra comunidad la oportunidad de navegar el sistema de salud y encontrar proveedores de salud que entiendan las necesidades de nuestras comunidades.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Las personas trans están siendo atacadas a nivel nacional y queremos que la ciudad de Nueva York siga liderando en términos de buenos servicios de afirmación de género.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Es una realidad que muchas de nuestras comunidades trans viajan de otros estados para servicios de afirmación de género.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Queremos que Nueva York sea el faro que guíe a nuestra comunidad al bienestar.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Todas las personas transgéneros o no binarias merecen una atención médica oportuna, asequible y que afirme su identidad, apoyando su bienestar físico y mental.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Instamos al Consejo a impulsar esas propuestas legislativas, a seguir invirtiendo en la atención comunitaria y a fortalecer la rendición de cuentas para que todos los neoyorquinos puedan acceder a la atención que merecen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alexia Sol
utterances.text: Gracias.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Gracias.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Quiero que todos escuchen tu testimonio, así que leeré la traducción.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I want everybody to hear your testimony, so I'm going to read the translation of it.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I'm going to skip the thank you to me and the committee.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Personally, when I was young, I did not have access to hormone therapy or surgeries, much less support.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I also did not have emotional support to transition, so I had to live a life that I did not really want.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: It is sad to say that I had two suicide attempts because I did not know how to navigate life as a trans woman, because I was living an identity in which I did not feel fulfilled or safe.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: This afternoon I am testifying because we want New York City to commit to being part of the change and ask you not to allow trans young people to live through what I experienced when I was young.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: May no trans child have to suffer and cry alone in a room because they do not have access to hormone therapy and support, especially from their family and health care specialists.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: These specialists, when they obtained their licenses, took a note to save lives instead of allowing a life to cease to exist.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Before denying access to hormone therapy to a trans person, think about what that person may be experiencing and thinking.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Perhaps what is in their mind is that there is no way out and that they cannot be who they really are.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And in any corner of the country or the world, a small human being may be thinking about giving up and ending their life today because society is denying them the right to live through their process of transformation and to be who they really are.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Today I want to speak directly to those trans young people who think they are alone.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I want to remind them that they are not, that they look at those of us who today have transitioned, that although it was not easy, at the end of the day our lives are similar.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: to the metamorphosis of a caterpillar that crawls and struggles against wind and tide, but one day that caterpillar becomes a beautiful butterfly.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: The coalition requests that the council continue investing in access to gender-affirming health care for uninsured and underinsured people, that LGBTQ plus community health organizations exist,

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: mental health services for young people, and that data collection respects privacy and helps identify gaps in services.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Coalition also strongly supports resolutions 547 and 208.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: These resolutions will provide our community with the opportunity to navigate the health care system and find health care providers who understand the needs of our communities.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Trans people are being attacked at the national level, and we want New York City to continue leading in terms of good gender-affirming services.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: It is a reality that many of our trans communities travel from other states to seek gender-affirming services.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: We want New York to be the beacon that guides our community toward well-being.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: All transgender and non-binary people deserve timely, affordable, and identity-affirming health care, supporting their physical and mental well-being.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: We urge the Council to advance these legislative proposals, continue investing in community care, and strengthen accountability so that all New Yorkers can access the care that they deserve.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Gracias.

chapters.summary: Brie Farron, a nurse practitioner at Planned Parenthood of Greater New York, says PPGNY conducted over 3,100 gender-affirming hormone therapy visits for over 1,500 people in 2025. She supports Intro 949, Res 208, and Res 547 and asks that Res 208 include nursing, pharmacy, and allied health students.
chapters.title: Planned Parenthood nurse practitioner Brie Farron describes affirming care and supports bills

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: Hello, my name is Brie Farron.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: My pronouns are she, her, and I'm a nurse practitioner at Planned Parenthood of Greater New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: Thank you to the chairs and the committees for convening this important hearing, and thank you to the bill sponsors who are advancing legislation to ensure that transgender, non-binary, and gender non-confirming youth have equitable access to the resources they need to live full lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: Planned Parenthood of Greater New York is a trusted provider of sexual and reproductive health care and education programs for communities throughout New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: In 2025, we conducted over 3,100 gender-affirming hormone therapy visits, providing care to over 1,500 individuals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: I've had the honor to provide care to many of those patients myself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: It has been my profound privilege to see the joy, comfort, and improved mental health that comes with accessing this life-affirming and life-saving care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: I've also bore witness as repeated attacks from the Trump-Vance administration cause increased anxiety, uncertainty, and despair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: We've seen the burden on patients trying to access care that has historically been out of reach and steeped in stigma and discrimination.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: Attacks nationwide that further limit access to compassionate, affordable, and comprehensive health care have forced many in the community to go without.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: It's imperative that New York remains a beacon for trans people seeking care, regardless of the federal political winds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: Planned Parenthood of Greater New York supports Intro 949, Resolution 208, and

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: Resolution 547, which ensure New York State and New York City are providing critical resources to transgender youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: We especially applaud Resolution 547, which establishes a gender-affirming care fund to provide financial support for the necessary medical and surgical care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: I personally hope that Resolution 208 can be expanded to include nursing, pharmacy, and allied health students as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: At PPGNY, we are dedicated to providing and protecting inclusive, affirming health care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: We commend the Council for advocating for the rights of all people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: New York must continue to protect our transgender youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: We look forward to continuing to work with the Council to ensure health care access for all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brie Farron
utterances.text: Thank you for your time and dedication to championing this issue.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Ronan Tuggle of the NYCLU says the organization has seen more intakes from trans New Yorkers and supportive parents seeking care, plus anecdotal reports of increased suicides. He supports Res 547 but wants the state definition of gender-affirming care expanded to mental health and other affirming care while excluding non-consensual intersex surgeries; supports Intro 949 with map safety concerns.
chapters.title: NYCLU's Ronan Tuggle reports uptick in trans intakes and seeks amendments

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: Good afternoon all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: Thanks so much for the chairs and the committees for holding this hearing today and giving us an opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: My name is Ronan Tuggle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: I use they, them pronouns.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: I'm the digital organizing strategist at the New York Civil Liberties Union, also known as NYCLU.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: With the federal attacks on gender-affirming care and hospitals'recent capitulation, the night clue has seen a tremendous uptick in the number of intakes we receive from trans New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: And disturbingly, we're also hearing anecdotally about an increase in suicides among trans people in the United States, which I know many folks have spoken to today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: The most common intake calls we field are from loving, supportive parents who are trying to figure out where they can access the health care their children rely on to thrive as their authentic selves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: Gender-affirming care is health care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: People seek it for all kinds of reasons, from precocious puberty to middle-aged hair loss to a diagnosis of gender dysphoria.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: This care is necessary for people to live in their bodies with dignity and health.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: When it comes to young people, every family should have the freedom to love and support their child, which includes the ability to make private medical decisions free from political interference.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: New York City and state have a role to play in ensuring New York remains a place where trans people can thrive, and the legislation the committee considers today is an important part of that project.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: The NYCLU strongly supports Resolution 5.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: which supports the creation of a state-level gender-affirming care access program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: This program would greatly support trans New Yorkers'ability to continue to access the health care we rely upon to be ourselves and chart our own futures.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: However, Resolution 547 includes a very narrow definition of gender-affirming care focusing entirely on medical care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: The resolution should be amended to reflect the state's definition of gender-affirming care, which also includes mental health care and other forms of affirming care, but also excludes non-consensual surgeries conducted on intersex young people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: The NYCLU also strongly supports Intro 949, although we do want to note some concerns around the MAP requirement, which could potentially put a target on the backs of gender-affirming care providers, especially in this political context.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: The state-level hospital transparency bill, currently A10203, Rozek in the Assembly and S8965, Hinchey in the

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: Senate, could serve as a model for a city-level legislation and help prospective patients identify where to find other frequently denied types of health care, such as reproductive health care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: Thank you so much for the opportunity to provide testimony and for your focus on supporting trans folks and access to gender-affirming care today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronan考
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you so much to all of you, and especially would love to have folks follow up on expanded definitions and other things to kind of strengthen the proposed legislation.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Everybody good?

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you so much.
