chapters.summary: Wren Galloway of the Ali Forney Center says gender-affirming care and mental health care cannot be separated. He describes barriers compounded by homelessness, immigration status, and unstable coverage, asks how the city measures access and protects privacy, and supports Intro 949 with updates and safeguards.
chapters.title: Wren Galloway describes compounded barriers for unhoused trans youth

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Caban, Perez, and all the other council members that are here with us today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: My name is Wren Galloway, and I serve as the Advocacy Manager at the LA4NA Center, which is the nation's largest provider for LGBTQ unhoused youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: Also a proud member of the NYC Trans and Queer Coalition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: I want to amplify what our other members said and really strongly amplify what the youth panel said as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: It was a really strong testimony from our youth and invite folks to really marinate in what they not only said, but listen and believe what they said as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: But what we know here is gender-affirming care is medically necessary, evidence-based health care recognized by every major medical association.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: We also cannot separate gender-affirming care from mental health care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: Without access to mental health care, we cannot fully support the mental health of transgender and gender nonconforming youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: And without accessible affirming care, we cannot fully support their gender-affirming expansion as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: As somebody that works with transgender and gender nonconforming youth all the time, as we had to unfortunately hear, we know that folks struggle with gender dysmorphia, things like suicide and amplified anxiety trying to receive these services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: So every day we try to work not to remove these opportunities from them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: So I simply wanted to invite people in to accept that these things are not only happening, but really think about how people are getting to their appointments, how people are understanding their identities as they're navigating these.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: healthcare systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: For many, there are barriers that are compounded by things like homelessness, immigration status, and unstable healthcare coverage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: Delays are interrupted, which really removes care and postpones treatment, which creates fear, uncertainty, and worsens mental health conditions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: As attacks continue in this country, I want to really invite us into a couple questions I have for council here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: So we can try to start to remove these gaps together.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: Are there enough affirming care providers to meet this demand?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: Which neighborhoods continue to lack services?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: How long are young people waiting for affirming mental health care?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: And how are the city agencies measuring whether access to gender-affirming care is improving in our health care systems?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: As New York continues to strengthen access to care, we encourage the city to continue to prioritize the strong privacy and security protections for those patients and health care professions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: In today's climate, these safeguards are being taken away, and these personal informations are essential to making sure people are protected.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: So I really want to just drop in lastly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: So the coalition is supporting Intro 949, but we need to make sure that not only is this resource regularly updated, but we need to make sure that there are barriers to care and making sure there are protections there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: So information alone is not enough, but making sure that that information is not being shared out to those that should not be receiving it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: It must be paired with continued investments in our provider's capacity, affirming mental health services and healthcare navigations, a community-based organization.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: organizations that young people already trust.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: Every transgender and gender non-conforming young person deserves timely, affordable, affirming care, as you all know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: So I appreciate your time today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wren Galloway
utterances.text: I will continue to add more into my written, but thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Biana Garcia of Make the Road New York and the NYC Trans and Queer Coalition says she injected hormones bought on the street at 17. She says many trans people still buy hormones and silicone on the black market and supports Intro 949, Res 208, and Res 547.
chapters.title: Biana Garcia describes buying hormones on black market and supports resource directory

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: And don't worry about my name.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: So thank you so much, Chair Tiffany Cavanaugh and Chair Narcisse and Farias and the New York City Council for holding this oversight hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: My name is Biana Garcia and I'm a community organizer with Make the Road New York and a member of New York Trans and Queer Coalition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: We are testifying before you this afternoon because we want to confirm our commitment to our communities and to highlight our needs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: As a transgender woman, access to gender-affirming care is vital because it helps us find guidance, information, and amplify our options for navigating the healthcare system in a way that is appropriate and safe for us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: I remember when I was 17 buying and injecting myself hormones that I buy from the street or from the black market.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: In my experience, it's not an isolated case.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: As a community organizer, I have heard many stories from community members about the lack of information and how difficult it is to find a gender-affirming care providers who understand respect and humanize of lives and our transition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: Gender-affirming care is medical necessary advanced-based healthcare recognized by all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: your medical association.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: Now, thanks to the leadership of New York City, I can say that I have a better chance to transition with my doctor guidance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: Trans people like me still face attacks on health care, but it's only in basic human rights across the country.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: In addition to that, trans people also face difficulties navigating the health system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: This virus is a gap to prevent the trans community from receiving the care that we deserve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: Our coalition also strongly supports 499, which co-established an LGBT directory as a trans woman working with my community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: Having a directory will help us facilitate and guide people toward healthy and safety transition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: We want also the city of New York to support Resolution 208 and 547.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: This resolution will help us as New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: To potentially those traveling from other states for access to better gender-affirming practice to ensure their names and pronouns are respected and feel safe when speaking with their doctors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: The New York has become a national leader in protecting transgender and non-binary communities, but this leadership is not only by law, but also people actually access to care they need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: And the reason why I'm saying this, I'm out of my script, but

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: I just want to say that it's important to continue talking about this issue because we have a lot of people, not only

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: people who were born in this country, but also people who are coming to New York to be who they want to be.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: People are still injecting the hormones that they buy from the street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: They also inject silicon from the black market.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: And we really need a health system that really supports everyone, doesn't matter gender or color, whatever it is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: So we're going to continue doing this work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: It was really so inspiring to see a lot of youth people here too.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Biana Garcia
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Raina Bien, board chair of Transformative Schools and parent of a nonbinary seventh grader, says her 12-year-old was kicked out of NYU, lost their doctor, and had records tied up in a lawsuit. She describes families driving hours or paying out of pocket for puberty blockers and asks the city to expand ages, train providers, and consider a city-run pediatric clinic.
chapters.title: Parent Raina Bien describes her nonbinary child losing NYU care

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raina Bien
utterances.text: My name is Raina Bien.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raina Bien
utterances.text: I'm the parent of a non-binary seventh grader and the board chair of Transformative Schools.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raina Bien
utterances.text: Thank you all for the opportunity to provide testimony today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raina Bien
utterances.text: The last couple of years have been very challenging for me and the other parents I know trying to raise happy, healthy trans children in a world that feels like it's been abruptly turned upside down.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raina Bien
utterances.text: My 12-year-old has been kicked out of NYU, lost the doctor to whom they confided deeply personal information, and had their medical records tied up in a lawsuit brought by our federal government.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raina Bien
utterances.text: The families that are struggling the hardest now are families like mine, with younger kids that need puberty blockers, the life-saving medications that put a temporary and reversible pause on puberty to give kids breathing room while they consider long-term medical decisions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raina Bien
utterances.text: Our families are locked out of the practices that have seemingly arbitrary age limits, like 16 or 14 or 13, as we learned when we called around, and that does include various H&H locations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raina Bien
utterances.text: We're driving multiple hours out of the city to clinics that have vowed they will keep going, paying out of pocket to private practitioners who don't take insurance in the hopes that will keep their practices safe,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raina Bien
utterances.text: anxiously navigating care with the overburdened local clinic that has too many patients, and in the case of too many families I know, moving abroad.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raina Bien
utterances.text: What does all this say about our city that calls itself a trans sanctuary, that has promised it will not turn its back on trans youth?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raina Bien
utterances.text: I applaud the City Council and Mayor's Office for promising more money for youth gender affirming care, but the details of how this money is spent is equally as important if it is to reach the most vulnerable population of younger trans children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raina Bien
utterances.text: Can you lean on the organizations already receiving city money to expand the ages they serve?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raina Bien
utterances.text: Can you provide funds for training new providers, including for puberty blocker implants?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raina Bien
utterances.text: If an H&H expansion is not on the table, then how about a city-run pediatric and teen clinic?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raina Bien
utterances.text: I urge you to think creatively with a bold new vision because pouring more money into how things have been done in the past will not solve our problems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raina Bien
utterances.text: We need new systems to keep children's care local, affordable, and protected from whatever the federal government plans next.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Raina Bien
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Kristen Clifford, mother of two trans kids, says NYU Langone ended health care for her teenager due to political pressure. She says DOJ requested their private records, NYU paid over $8 million and stopped medically necessary care, and puberty blocker implants are hard to access due to insurance coding; she urges the city to attract and support affirming practitioners.
chapters.title: Parent Kristen Clifford says NYU ended care under political pressure

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: Hi, my name is Kristen Clifford and my pronouns are she, her, and I am the proud mom of two trans kids, one of whom is still a minor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: NYU Langone ended healthcare for my teenager, not because of medical science, but because of political pressure from the Trump administration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: Our family's private medical records have been requested by Trump's Department of Justice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: We have that injunction for now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: NYU's recent deal with Trump's Department of Justice is a shakedown, and NYU paid over $8 million and stopped medically necessary health care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: This is the environment that we are all living in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: I am so grateful that both of my children were able to receive excellent gender-affirming health care at NYU, and especially puberty blockers, and especially these puberty blocker implants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: Having that time is so important to early teenagers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: I cannot stress this enough.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: And puberty blockers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: and especially the implant, has been one of the things that parents struggle to access the most in the past few years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: I do believe some of it is because of the way that it has been coded by insurance companies, where it used to be in office and now it is coded as surgery.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: And if there's anything that the city can do, we would appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: Our care was taken away twice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: After the first time, it was restored.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: And then again, as I was protesting in Washington, D.C., some of us were arrested.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: And as I got out of jail for protesting to gender-affirming care, I got a message saying that NYU had cut my child's gender-affirming care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: We need the city and state to do everything they can to support trans kids.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: My children's mental health was greatly improved by gender-affirming care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: I have watched them blossom and grow and become their true selves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: The fascist dictatorial federal government is attacking our children and our families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: The political environment is harming our children, causing anxiety, fear, and despair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: And parents know what it is like to try to keep our kids alive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: And not all of our kids make it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: A teenager in my neighborhood in Queens committed suicide by jumping off the Queens

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: a few years ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: They had been bullied for being trans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: We need to do everything in our power to support trans kids, especially in light of the harmful federal actions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: And we need to step in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: The city needs to step in and provide gender-affirming care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: One of my questions for the city is how can the city attract

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: Even get tissues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: How can the city attract and support more gender-affirming care practitioners?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: This is something that we need as a sanctuary city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: Gender-affirming care is life-saving care because I've seen that up close in my own home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: Trans kids need all the support they can get to become trans adults.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: And parents need support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: So many parents are scared to reach out because of all of the anti-trans rhetoric and hatred.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: They're scared to get help for their families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: This resource map is really important because we share information in a whisper network.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: But then if we have this research map, this resource map, we are all worried about the providers and about the safety and about families who, families don't come forward because they're afraid of being doxxed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: I'm grateful, I'm so grateful to all the people who are here today supporting trans youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: And I support

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: All that New York City can do to do gender-affirming health care access.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Cabán thanks the panel, especially the parents, and asks if they want to expand on how the city can support their families. Kristen Clifford says their kids are lucky to have them, but the city must support kids who do not have supportive parents.
chapters.title: Cabán thanks parent witnesses and invites further suggestions

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I want to thank you all for your testimony, especially for the parents that we have with us.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: You have provided us with

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: what we've needed to hear, but also suggestions on what could come next.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And so I just want to create another space if there's anything that you want to expand on in terms of how else the city can support you and your families at this time.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And obviously our door is open and we want to be having those conversations.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And also, my God, y'all are incredible parents.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: So thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: You know what?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: Our kids are lucky because they have us, and there's so many kids that don't have parents like us, and the city needs to support all of those kids.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: JJ Cleo Mizrahi says trans people are dehumanized and stigmatized, causing fear around taking hormones and facing harassment. Mizrahi says gender care includes support groups, counseling, and social services, describes discrimination in a union and a psych ward, and supports the resource map.
chapters.title: JJ Cleo Mizrahi describes trans fear, discrimination, and class barriers to care

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: My name is Jajay Cleo Mizrahi, and I'm a longtime New Yorker, and I use they or they.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: Every time I come here to City Hall, when we are talking about measures that are affecting the most marginalized, it's usually in the end after corporate interests.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: I really appreciate everyone who's still here, but we know that it's a challenge to wait when not all of the City Hall, especially those who are trans allies that really need to hear the testimony of those of us who are struggling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: I'm going to do my best to go through, and I also sent a written testimony as well, as I wasn't feeling well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: We know that trans people are being dehumanized and stigmatized across America and across the world as punching bags.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: And that even as a trans adult, I know that for my inner child and for trans youth that I am protecting, it is crippling my mental health.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: Living with hysteria and fear of thinking, even today, if I take my hormones, am I going to be targeted?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: Am I going to be mocked?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: Am I going to be harassed again on the subway and the train?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: Am I going to be mocked and denied care while in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: And so on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: We know that gender care is more than just surgeries or HRT, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: It's support groups.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: It's counseling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: It's social services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: These are all the elements that people are forgetting that encompasses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: gender-affirming care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: And I'm only here because of trans ancestors who paved the way, but we know that we're still struggling here in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: When I was working at the New York Public Library during COVID, not only was I discriminated on the basis of gender and my disabilities, but DC 37, the largest union

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: for the city, did not even have any trans-affirming care that I had to pay out of pocket during the pandemic and was not even trans-competent, and I had to keep re-explaining myself to my union member.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: I come from a tradition that says if you save a life, you save the world, and that you're able to break any rule in the Torah as long as you save a life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: And that is part of what's bringing me here today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: We know that trans people are facing, even in New York City, systematic barriers for jobs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: So thinking about accounting, about how much it is, to think, how much am I going to pay for food today, or my hormones, and having to check.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: We know that three out of five LGBT adults are without food, and that is proven from HRA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: When I was detained and denied certain care in a psych ward for just walking while trans in one of your city hospitals, I had a relapse because I was not given certain medication and just like my hormonal treatment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: Let me just continue to go through my story.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: We know that it's hard enough to communicate our needs when both in city council and in state, we still do not have

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: One TGNCI elected official.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: And I hope that I'll be part of a generation that will break that glass ceiling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: We know that with FBI, the hate crimes of trans women of color at 79%, more than any other marginalized demographic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: We have went yesterday to even rally against Mount Sinai and NYU, and they are debating, do we care more about our values or do we care more about our money to cave into Trumpism?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: I could go on and on and on, but I even just wanted to just be able to think about those who are most vulnerable, again, that were here for youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: If you even spend an evening at Black Trans Liberation Kitchen, on average, they have 200 trans youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: Most are malnourished.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: Most are forced into sex work here in New York City and are not always getting HRT by approved medical care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: And we know from our elders who are not even here, what does it mean when we do not have medical care that is proper?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: I'm going to be here around afterwards, but I just wanted to be able to remind you that, again, even for those of us who are able to get some aspects of our gender care approving, that still gender care, some aspects are really class-based.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: There's, just for even a letter for FFS, I had to wait over five years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: Certain operations and care, like vocal feminization, is for those with certain types of insurances.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: So I really wanted to put into a factor that this is affecting trans people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: people across generations, and thank you so much for being here.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And we'll be sure to read the full of your written testimony you submitted.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Annabelle Ruggiero says she helped organize the Mount Sinai protest and thanks Director Brown for attending. She supports Intro 949 but says such steps should have happened earlier, blames collective inaction, and demands public consequences for Mount Sinai and NYU, financial support for institutions that stand by patients, and taxing the rich to offset federal health care cuts.
chapters.title: ACT UP organizer Annabelle Ruggiero demands consequences for hospitals that folded

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: Hello everyone, I'm Annabelle Ruggiero.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: I'm strictly speaking on behalf of myself today, but I am an ACT UP rabble rouser who helped organize the protest at Mount Sinai that Director Brown spoke at.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: And I'd like to take the opportunity to thank her publicly for being there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: To start, today's hearing and bills are great steps.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: Intro 949 fulfills a demand our community has been asking for.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: As someone who had the opportunity to advocate for this kind of resource, I'd like to personally thank Councilmember Shulman and her staff.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: But these are steps that need to happen over a year ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: The situation has, quite predictably, deteriorated rapidly over the past year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: A few short months ago, the governor became the likely culprit behind appropriations for gender-affirming care being cut from the state budget, and now two hospitals have folded to fascist inquisition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: I must admit, I am personally invested in inflicting political and reputational damage on both Mount Sinai and NYU Langone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: And yet, I find it hard to lay blame fully at their feet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: At the end of the day, they made a cruel calculation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: Either defy the feral government and rely on insufficient municipal funds to make up the difference, or abandon trans youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: The context in local policy

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: the environment these calculations were made under is due to a collective failure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: To be blunt, this is the fault of the relative inaction by the state government, the city council, and both recent mayoralities, Adams and Mamdani.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: Not them personally, but their mayoralities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: So, while I am happy with the legislation before us today, we demand more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: We demand far more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: We need to make a public example of both Mount Sinai and NYU Langone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: We need to financially support institutions who stand by their patients.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: We need every fascist capitulator to know that the support of the people is predicated on them not folding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: We need a taxable rich to make up for federal cuts to everyone's health care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: And in these bleak times, we need you, the mayorality, the governor, and the AG to be proactive instead of reactive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annabelle Ruggiero
utterances.text: For a more concrete idea of what we can do, no more municipal funds to any discriminatory health care institutions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Rae Blazin, a public health professional testifying personally, says an LGBTQ resource map already exists at DOHMH. Blazin says Intro 949 would codify and protect it and allow greater provider granularity, and describes needing word-of-mouth after a provider left NYU; supports the map with provider safety and an implementation timeline.
chapters.title: Rae Blazin supports expanded, codified DOHMH LGBTQ resource map

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: Hi, my name is Rae Blazin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: My pronouns are they, them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: I have served as a public health professional for the city and social services, serving the LGBTQ and unhoused community before, but I am testifying today in a personal capacity, and the views expressed are my own regarding Intro 949.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: An LGBTQ resource map does exist at DUHMH.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: This was addressed earlier.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: However, not only will this particular bill codify and protect its existence, which is necessary in times in which our access to our own health is becoming more and more difficult to access across the country,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: but it also leaves room for greater granularity when it comes to reliable information about individual providers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: This map, becoming a more concrete and expanded resource, has the potential to be a life-saving mechanism by increasing accessibility through readily available information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: As somebody who recently had their provider leave their practice at NYU Langone, at a clinic that was previously an all-queer local clinic that had been bought out by NYU,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: knowing I was a patient in a practice where some providers would be supportive of my identity and work with me to provide me with specialty knowledge about my own health, and that some would not be suited for that endeavor, was anxiety-inducing and made me reticent to seek care

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: and resulted in the disruption of my care for both ordinary wellness and for chronic conditions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: I had to rely on word of mouth and quietly speaking to other staff members in the hallways to get

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: gather office opinion on who would be outfitted to respectfully tend to my health care needs for a long-term, reliable, and culturally responsive provider to a queer and transgender person.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: Having a map expanded with the weight of DOHMH and the city's authority and consideration of standards behind it, and with care and regard for provider safety in turn,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: would make the inevitable repeat of that situation, because it will happen again to me at some point.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: Sooner, I hope later.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: But it will make that experience a lot smoother and more accessible and reduce meaningful barriers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: This can also potentially reduce siloing of care to specific institutions, many of which are Manhattan-based that are already listed, who strain to serve the sheer number of people who require safer services and provide an invaluable resource to many other New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: There is also, I do want to put forward for consideration the fact that the bill as it stands does not have a time span indicated on what would be a reasonable implementation time on that map.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: And given that it is unclear if the existing map is being amended or if a new one is being created, I do think a lifetime on that, what that can look like would be appropriate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rae Blazin
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

chapters.summary: Kimberly Blair of Girls for Gender Equity says about 1 in 5 TGNCNBI youth report attempting suicide and nearly 50% seriously consider it. She says anti-trans laws increased suicide attempts by as much as 72% in restrictive states, and Intro 949 would relieve community organizations of updating resource lists; supports all three bills.
chapters.title: Girls for Gender Equity's Kimberly Blair links affirming environments to lower suicide attempts

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: Good afternoon and thank you Chairs Caban, Farias, and Narcisse and members here today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: I am Kimberly Blair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: I'm the Senior Director of Policy and Advocacy at Girls for Gender Equity, an organization that works intergenerationally through a black feminist lens to center the leadership of black girls and gender expansive youth of color.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: At a time when trans and non-binary people are under nationwide attack, GGE stands firmly here today on behalf of our BIPOC, trans and gender expansive youth of color.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: We stand also as a member of the NYC Trans and Queer Coalition to support Intro 949, Resos 208, and 547, which we see as stepping stones towards increasing access to life-saving care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: As someone who has spent the majority of her career at the intersections of reproductive justice and mental health policy, I'm here to tell you that an estimated 1 in 5 TNGC

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: NBI youth report attempting suicide, and that nearly 50% seriously consider attempting suicide within any given one-year period.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: In past years, the increase in anti-trans laws in 19 restrictive states have significantly increased incidents of past year suicide attempts among these youth by as much as 72%.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: While New Yorkers might think we're immune,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: because we don't live in one of these restrictive states, our TGNC MBI youth consume this anti-trans rhetoric and experience bans right here from trusted healthcare facilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: Conversely, the NIH reports TGNC MBI youth who have high social support and gender-affirming environments report suicide attempt rates at less than half the rate of those without.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: We believe these bills are interventions that would help us increase the social support necessary to combat these negative mental health outcomes among our youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: Intro 949 especially would help organizations like mine from spending a fair amount of staff time creating and updating our own internal resources annually to support gender expansive youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: We don't see this as the complete responsibility of CBOs to do this while also navigating one-to-one case management,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: supporting students'financial and immigration needs, and providing life-saving education and programming to aid TGNC-MBI youth's self-discovery and identity formation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: Due to time restrictions, we plan to submit the rest of our commentary via written, including suggested bill edits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: But I want to thank you again for taking the time today to listen to and stand up for as allies to our TGNCMBI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kimberly Blair
utterances.text: We hope that you vote these bills favorably out of committee.

chapters.summary: Cabán appreciates Mizrahi's comments about faith and saving a life. Mizrahi describes growing up in the Orthodox Jewish community, family rejection, internalized negative messages, and says the trans community remains on guard and fearful until Trumpism ends.
chapters.title: Cabán and JJ Cleo Mizrahi discuss faith, family rejection, and trans visibility

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And I just want to take a moment to say I appreciate what you said about your faith.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: One of the things I love about the Jewish faith is the idea that none of us is beyond redemption.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And yeah, when you save a life, you save the world.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And going beyond that, I think about the way that these institutions have capitulated.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And another part of the Jewish faith is like, you don't sacrifice it.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: It's like we get there together or we don't get there at all.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And so I think it's really, really powerful that you all are here and making it clear that.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: that's the case.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And so I'm really proud to be fighting with y'all.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: So I appreciate you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Yeah, go for it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: Yeah, I just, it's always hard to like time consume with everything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: But, you know, I'm thinking about also as someone who grew up in New York, who did not know about my rights and about accessing certain safe spaces, you know, about how, for example, growing up in the Orthodox Jewish community, there's misinformation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: When I came out, my mother said to me, not long ago, she says, all you'll ever be is a prostitute.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: And my father said, all you'll ever be, no one will ever love you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: And these are messages we're internalizing that they are taking from the media, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: And I had to make a really hard predicament over a decade ago where my mother said, either you comply to my rules despite paying the rent and able by law to, you know, not have to

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: observe her faith, you know, because we have a different Jewish denomination.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: She said, either you have to take your hormones and you have to leave or you don't.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: And, you know, I was subjected to abuse for many years and never got help.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: And this is the reality for many people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: And there's so many stories of people who, whether they leave a fundamentalist faith or whether they're not in a supportive

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: environment, and what does that do to them long term about having internalized about who they are and feeling fearful that you're hated and that you're paranoid.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: And it's still even hard, I'll just end, with trans elders to remind you that not everyone's against you, but I will say that everyone in the community is on guard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: And it breaks my heart to even go to a support group and see people terrified of just simply wanting to change other parts of their documentation and feel like we have to hide until the Trumpism is over.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - JJ Cleo Mizrahi
utterances.text: So thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kristen Clifford
utterances.text: Thank you all.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: All right.

chapters.summary: Angelica Jadunandan, mother of an eight-year-old transgender daughter, says her family moved from Florida to Brooklyn for legal protections. She describes learning that trans kids do best when loved and supported, hopes affirming care remains available if needed, and urges New York City to remain a beacon.
chapters.title: Parent Angelica Jadunandan says family moved from Florida for her trans daughter

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: My name is Angelica Jadunandan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: I use she, her pronouns, and I'm the mother of an eight-year-old transgender daughter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: Three years ago, my family moved from Florida to Brooklyn in search of the legal protections New York offers transgender people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: I'm now a member of District 15's Community Education Council and an organizer with parents of gender expansive kids.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: I grew up in a conservative Christian home and knew nothing about transgender people when my daughter told me she was a girl at three years old.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: She didn't say, I think I'm a girl or I wish I was a girl.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: She said, I am a girl.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: So I listened and I learned.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: I joined parent groups, bought the books, and read the research.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: And what I found was remarkably simple.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: Trans kids have the best outcomes when they're loved and supported.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: Along the way, I also encountered a lot of confusing rhetoric about trans youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: To clear things up, my daughter isn't a girl trapped in a boy's body.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: She's a girl who was born into a world that decided she was a boy before she could speak for herself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: We put children into one of two boxes before they're ever even born and expect them to spend their lives fitting into them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: But gender, biology, and nature are far more complicated than that, and it's precisely that diversity that brings beauty to our world.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: My daughter knows she doesn't need to look or dress a certain way to be a girl.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: In fact, she prefers shopping in the boys'section because that's where she finds the video game shirts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: And above all others, the title she claims is a gamer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: I don't know whether my daughter will ever need gender-affirming medical care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: She's only eight years old.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: She also has several medical conditions that require us to see multiple specialists.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: And as her mother, I selfishly hope that she won't have to navigate any more medical challenges.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: But if gender-affirming care is something she needs to feel safe, comfortable, and fully herself in a world that constantly tells her she can't be, we need that option to be on the table.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: My family came to New York City because we believed our daughter would be protected here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: Families across this country have looked to New York City as a beacon of hope where their children can live freely and access the care they need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: It's up to all of us to make sure this city remains that place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Andy Bowen of the Queer Budget Center and an H&H patient says the Trump administration loses when challenged and that the city should align the Law Department, chief counsel, and corporation counsel to protect affirming care under the Human Rights Act. Bowen says city contracts with hospital systems give leverage to compel continuity of care and supports the bills.
chapters.title: Andy Bowen urges whole-of-government approach and city contract leverage

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: Good afternoon, chairs at Cabana and Farias, members of the Committee of Women and Gender Equity and Mental Health and Substance Use.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: My name is Andy Bowen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: I am founder and executive director of a now year-old-ish organization called Queer Budget Center, a national organization that uses government budget advocacy to strengthen vulnerable communities'material resources.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: I miss working with you all and have joined the MIC Trans and Queer Coalition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: I'm also a proud gender-affirming care patient at NYC Health and Hospitals, which has provided me the best care of my life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: I co-signed the asks and questions of the NYC Trans and Queer Coalition partners, and I will emphasize some extra points.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: It's important to note, given the capitulation of Mount Sinai, NYU, and Presbyterian, that the Trump admin loses when challenged, and other hospital systems have put up fights, notably in the Midwest.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: It's notable that after many losses in court, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services have held off finalizing their proposed rule that would condition hospitals'participation in Medicare and Medicaid on its offering of gender-affirming care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: With that in mind, we need a whole-of-government approach to fight the feds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: I look to the entire Mamdani administration, including the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: law department, chief counsel, and corporation at council to align on a unified goal of protecting gender-affirming care in line with the New York City Human Rights Act,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: actions of the Attorney General and other AGs across the nation who not only hold the Trump administration to account, but in many cases hold their own health care systems to account.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: And yes, I recognize the state is the regulator for hospitals, but the city has a lot of leverage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: The city holds contracts with these health systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: These contracts are in many cases for important services that shouldn't be ended or interrupted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: However, the funding gives more leverage for the city to hold these systems to the city's human rights laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: The city should use that power to compel continuation of care for trans and gender nonconforming people to the extent legally possible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: As to the bills, I support them and will provide feedback in my written testimony, which will be submitted after the fact.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: On Reso 547, the governor must follow the example of city council and the mayor in making historic investments in gender-affirming care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: The community is suffering and waiting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: I cannot echo hard enough also the need to expand gender-affirming care for all ages and that care needs to be widely geographically accessible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: The city as a government has the resources and we have the law on our side.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Cabán asks whether there are other things the city should do. Angelica Jadunandan asks for LGBTQ+ representation in mandated curricula and school-level family support; Andy Bowen declines to elaborate but offers to follow up. Cabán thanks them.
chapters.title: Cabán asks final in-person panel for additional city support ideas

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I appreciate you so much.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I appreciate you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I just, again, want to provide an opportunity to both of you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: If there are other things beyond what you stated in your testimony that you think the city can or should be doing to support you and your families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: So I work on the CEC and we've been talking about mandated curricula and right now one of the programs is Wit and Wisdom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: There's no LGBTQ plus representation in that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: Teachers, if they choose to teach,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: they have to supplement that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: They have to rework the whole lesson plan to include that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: And then it also, it changes from school to school.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: Do you have a supportive principle?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: We have guidelines in New York City that protect these kids, but it's not always

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: the case that they're followed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: And so just making sure that our kids are learning about, I mean, for my daughter to learn about people like herself

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angelica Jadunandan
utterances.text: and to make sure that families are receiving support at the school level too, not just medical.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Yeah, thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: I am so overwhelmed with too many thoughts, and I am afraid of saying the wrong thing right now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: We'll talk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: We'll talk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: Having been a former, worked for the previous administration, I feel like I know too much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: So I'll step back.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: We were very glad you were there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: Oh, thanks.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andy Bowen
utterances.text: I'm not sure I was.

chapters.summary: Cabán says the hearing will move to Zoom and calls Suheili Mendez. Staff tells the witness she may begin.
chapters.title: Cabán moves to Zoom testimony and calls Suhali Méndez

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Okay, so we're going to move to Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I think we have one person on the Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Suheili Mendez.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Suhali Méndez of New York Lawyers for the Public Interest describes the UndocuCare TGNCI+ program serving transgender, gender nonconforming, and intersex immigrants. She says immigrant youth face trauma, language barriers, misinformation, and fear of government institutions; supports Intro 949, Res 208, and Res 547 and will submit detailed testimony.
chapters.title: NYLPI's Suhali Méndez supports bills for immigrant TGNCI youth access

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Chair Caban, Chair Farias, and members of the committees.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: My name is Suhali Mendez, and I'm the Policy and Legislative Coordinator at New York Lawyers for the Public Interest, or better known as NILP.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: NILPI is a civil rights organization that advances justice for people with disabilities, immigrants, communities of color, and other historically marginalized communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: And through our UndocuCare TGNCI Plus program, we work directly with transgender, gender nonconforming, and intersex immigrants,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: including young people and their families, to help them access health care, housing, as well as legal services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Thank you so much for holding this very important hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: NILPI is proud to support INCHO 949, RESO 208, and RESO 547, all of which are important steps toward

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: improving access to health care and mental health outcomes for transgender and non-binary New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: At a time when transgender and non-binary youth face growing barriers to health care across the country, New York City has an opportunity as well as a responsibility to continue leading.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Access to gender-affirming care is not only a health care issue, it is a civil right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: rights issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Every young person deserves access to care that respects their identity, protects their dignity,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: as well as supports their physical and mental health being.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Transgender non-binary youth experience disproportionately high rates of depression, anxiety, and suicides.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: These outcomes are not caused simply by a young person's gender identity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Rather, they're often the result of discrimination, stigma, bullying, family rejection, as well as systematic barriers that make it harder to access health care and support services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: These barriers often are greater within immigrant youth, particularly those who are undocumented and seeking asylum.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Many of these individuals and families we work with has fled violence and persecution because of their gender identity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: They frequently face significant trauma while also navigating complex health care, housing, and immigration systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Fear of government institutions, misinformation about eligibility of services, language barriers, and experiences of discrimination can prevent people from accessing the care that they need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: That is why the legislation before the Council today is so important.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Incho 949 will require the creation of LGBTQI plus health and gender affirming care resources, including a searchable provider directory.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Too many families spend...

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Time is up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Expired.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: You can finish your thought.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: No, finish your thought.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: You're good.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: My man's just doing his job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Noted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: So we support Intro 949.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: We also support Reso 208, which recognizes the critical role and bias that continues to play in healthcare settings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Anti-bias trainings for medical students can provide future providers to better serve transgender, non-binary patients, immigrants, and people with disabilities and other historically marginalized communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: And lastly, we support Razo 547, which calls for the establishment of gender-affirming care program within New York State Department of Health to help ensure continuity of care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Consistent access to medically necessary health care is essential for many immigrants'patients.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Disruptions in housing, insurance coverage, or access to providers can make continuity to care particularly difficult.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: And I will be providing more detailed testimony for record.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: And I thank you so much for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I also want to thank Director Brown for staying here for the entirety of the public testimony.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you for being here.

chapters.summary: Cabán says she wants every trans child to grow up to be a trans elder, able to play, make friends, engage in sports, build a family, and enjoy New York City. She thanks everyone for the shared commitment and closes the hearing.
chapters.title: Cabán closes with call for trans children to grow up as trans elders

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And I want to close by saying it is really, really simple.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I want, we want every trans child to grow up to be a trans elder, period.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And I want those kids to be able to play, to make friends, to engage in sports, to build whatever kind of family they choose to build in and to enjoy.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: What I view as the best city on the planet.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: So I just, I've been really moved by the testimony today and all of our shared commitment to really looking out for each other.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I know that there is a lot more that government needs to do and we're here to fight to be able to do that.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And just thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And I don't know if, Chair, you have anything else.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And with that, we close today's hearing.

summary: Joint oversight hearing of the Committees on Hospitals, Mental Health and Substance Use, and Women and Gender Equity on access to gender-affirming care and mental health outcomes for transgender and nonbinary youth.

Administration testimony came from the Mayor's Office of LGBTQIA+ Affairs, NYC Health and Hospitals, and DOHMH, covering clinical evidence, federal pressure, hospital capitulations, city investments, provider training, and Health Map resources.

Public testimony included youth, advocates, providers, and parents supporting Intro 949, Res 208, and Res 547, with repeated calls for expanded access, privacy protections, provider capacity, and continuity of care.
title: Committee on Hospitals
topic: Oversight - Access to Gender-Affirming Care and Associated Mental Health Outcomes for Transgender and Nonbinary Youth
